section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, your following distance should increase and the chance of a fatality in a crash increases.,b:Increasing speed reduces stopping distance.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the severity of crashes; therefore you should increase following distance as speed increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck carrying flammable liquids, what precaution should you take at railroad crossings?
options: a:Pass the vehicle on the right if you are in a hurry.,b:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.,c:Assume the vehicle will always follow the speed limit.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad tracks before crossing. Always be prepared to stop when following these vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting an alley or driveway across a sidewalk, what should you do with regard to pedestrians?
options: a:Stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are in the sidewalk.
note: When leaving a driveway or alley, stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to any pedestrians and traffic.

question: When is it necessary to use your low-beam headlights?
options: a:In fog.,b:On a lighted street.,c:On a freeway.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, snow, or mist because high beams reflect off precipitation and can reduce visibility.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you at a safe following distance?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and signal your intentions in advance.,b:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Brake suddenly to create distance.,d:Tailgate the car ahead to discourage them from following.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early helps the driver behind judge a safe following distance and react appropriately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the center of the roadway has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are in a passing zone and may pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are allowed only to make right turns in this area.
note: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, passing is permitted from your lane when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and allow the other vehicle to pass safely.,b:Brake hard to prevent them from passing.,c:Speed up to block the pass.
note: When being passed, maintain your speed or slow slightly if needed to allow the vehicle to complete the pass safely; do not speed up.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels on the drug for warnings about driving.,b:Drink alcohol to counteract drowsiness.,c:Continue to drive regardless of any warnings.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while using the medicine.

question: Which is true about driving while taking medications?
options: a:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b:Over-the-counter meds cannot impair driving if taken correctly.,c:All prescribed medicines are always safe for driving.
note: Many over-the-counter and prescription medicines can impair driving; always check labels and consult your doctor or pharmacist.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?
options: a:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone.' (reduce speed and be careful in work zones).,b:Fines are the same as normal traffic fines.,c:Only slow down if you see workers present.
note: Slow for Cone Zone safety campaigns: reduce speed and be prepared for changing conditions and workers.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Accelerate quickly once the bus stops.
note: Even after the bus lights are off and the arm is retracted, watch for children who may walk into the roadway before moving on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, what should you do before entering the interstate?
options: a:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: When no acceleration lane exists, wait for a safe gap and then accelerate to merge smoothly; do not use the shoulder to accelerate onto the interstate.

question: Any activity that causes you to ____ can lead to a crash.
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your attention away from driving,c:Take your eyes off the road
note: Distractions that take your attention, eyes, or hands away from driving significantly increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always travel at what speed?
options: a:A speed appropriate for road, weather, and traffic conditions and within legal limits.,b:At the posted maximum no matter the conditions.,c:At the speed of the vehicles immediately surrounding you even if over the limit.
note: Adjust your speed to the conditions; never drive above legal limits and slow down when road or weather conditions are poor.

question: When driving in fog, which headlight setting is best?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Low beams reduce glare and reflection in fog; high beams reflect and can reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does 'yield' also mean you must stop if you cannot merge safely?
options: a:True — you must stop if you cannot merge into the flow of traffic safely.,b:False — yielding never requires stopping.,c:Only if signs say to stop.,d:Only at railroad crossings.
note: If you cannot safely merge when required to yield, you must stop and wait for a safe gap in traffic.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Cell phones and other devices divert attention from driving and greatly increase crash risk.

question: On roadways, bicycles are legally considered:
options: a:Vehicles with the same traffic rights and duties as motor vehicles.,b:Hazards that must always yield.,c:Objects that are not regulated.,d:Pedestrians.
note: Bicyclists are treated as vehicles and must follow the same rules as drivers of motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which of these locations?
options: a:On hills and curves where visibility is limited.,b:At all intersections regardless of visibility.,c:Only at highway on-ramps.
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, intersections, or other places where you cannot see ahead far enough to pass safely.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off rapidly to warn the other driver.
note: When blinded by oncoming lights, look toward the right edge of the road and use the lane markings to guide you until the vehicle passes.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Limit driving to weekdays.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,d:Drive slower than the speed limit.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective measure to reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash.

question: When approaching a flashing yellow arrow for a left turn, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Turn left without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before turning.

question: A dashed line separating lanes indicates:
options: a:You may pass when it is safe.,b:You may not pass.,c:Both lanes travel the same direction (always).
note: A broken (dashed) line allows passing when it is safe to do so, provided there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Is it true that every motor vehicle in Maine must have liability insurance?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only trucks must have insurance.
note: Maine law requires that every motor vehicle operated on public roads be covered by motor vehicle liability insurance.

question: Road surfaces are most slippery during what time?
options: a:Just after it begins to rain.,b:After heavy rain has washed oils away for hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads can become especially slick just after rain begins when oil and residue mix with water; exercise extra caution.

question: A "No passing zone" sign indicates:
options: a:You must maintain a steady speed.,b:It is unsafe and illegal to pass in that area.,c:That you should speed up slightly to merge.
note: No passing zone signs are posted where visibility or conditions make passing unsafe and prohibited.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden moves.,b:Beep your horn to warn the child away.,c:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; slow down, give extra space, and be prepared for sudden changes in direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, how should you merge?
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then merge.
note: Choose a gap that allows you to accelerate to the speed of traffic while merging safely into the lane.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing warning signals, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Look for a train, then speed up.,c:Stop and look for a train.
note: If electric or mechanical signals are warning of a train, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and only proceed when it is safe.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as your speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:The tires become less effective at dispersing water and may hydroplane.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on wet pavement, tires may lose their ability to clear water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Broken yellow lines are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and permit passing where safe.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Indicate no passing zones.
note: Yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic; a dashed line means passing is allowed when safe.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,b:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If another driver is tailgating you, create extra space ahead of your vehicle and avoid braking suddenly — slow gradually or change lanes to reduce collision risk.

question: If you are facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Proceed because vehicles have the right-of-way.,c:Make pedestrians wait until you pass.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in the intersection, including when turning on a steady green signal.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), should you immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:False – you should avoid immediately slamming the brakes.,b:True – quickly apply the brakes to stop the skid.
note: If hydroplaning, try to regain control by releasing the accelerator and steering smoothly; immediate hard braking can worsen the skid.

question: Before starting the engine, you should ensure:
options: a:You and all passengers have fastened their seat belts.,b:Only rear-seat passengers are belted.,c:Only child passengers are belted.
note: Develop a habit of buckling your safety belt and ensuring all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and yield to them.,b:Honk to warn them to get out of the way.,c:Proceed because they have no right-of-way.,d:Speed up to pass before they reach you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be; stop and let them cross safely.

question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be within what distance of the curb?
options: a:18 inches or less.,b:14 inches.,c:6 inches.
note: When parallel parked, your wheels should be no more than 18 inches from the curb so the vehicle is safely positioned.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, blind spots remain; glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check them.

question: As a pedestrian, you should:
options: a:Never enter a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Always insist on right-of-way regardless of distance.,c:Enter crosswalks anytime since drivers must stop.
note: Even though pedestrians have priority in crosswalks, do not step into traffic if vehicles are too close to stop safely.

question: To help ensure your physical condition doesn't make you an unsafe driver, you should:
options: a:Know how medications affect your driving and drive within your limitations.,b:Only drive when you feel fully rested without medical checkups.,c:Ignore minor physical issues while driving.
note: Be aware of how medicines and your physical fitness affect driving. Keep within your limitations and consult medical professionals as needed.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can lower your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:It decreases your chance of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Emotional stress reduces concentration and driving performance; avoid driving if you are emotionally unstable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to make a left turn at a green light but heavy oncoming traffic prevents it. What should you do?
options: a:Wait behind the crosswalk until traffic clears, or use the next intersection if necessary.,b:Wait in the middle of the intersection until there is a gap.,c:Proceed and turn when you see an opening.
note: If oncoming traffic prevents a safe left turn, wait behind the crosswalk until traffic clears; do not block the intersection.

question: Roads are especially slippery just after rain begins. When roads are slippery you should:
options: a:Avoid making sharp turns or abrupt stops at high speeds.,b:Test tire traction by accelerating quickly uphill.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead.
note: Reduce speed and make smooth steering and braking inputs to avoid skids on newly wet roads.

question: A key trait of a good defensive driver is to:
options: a:Watch for and anticipate the actions of other drivers.,b:Drive slowly at all times.,c:Maintain a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: Defensive drivers stay alert to the actions of others and anticipate potential problems to avoid crashes.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Slow speeds.,c:Night driving.
note: Higher speeds extend stopping distances and dramatically increase crash severity; adjust speed appropriately.

question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, yellow, red.
note: Traffic lights are vertically ordered from top to bottom as red, yellow, then green.

question: Which factor does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,d:Roadway surface condition.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, speed, vehicle weight, brakes, tires, and road conditions, but not the time of day.

question: What color are regulatory signs typically?
options: a:White with black, red, or green letters or symbols.,b:Green with white letters.,c:Yellow with black letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of laws that must be obeyed and are commonly white rectangles with black, red, or green markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Yield only to traffic approaching from the right.,d:Ignore it if the road looks clear.
note: When approaching a yield sign, you must yield to traffic already in the lane you intend to enter; be prepared to stop if needed.

question: When an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,c:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it goes by.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right edge of the road and stop to clear the path; on one-way streets, pull toward the nearest edge.

question: Which action helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure your tires have good tread depth.,b:Ensure your tires are overinflated.,c:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, keep tires in good condition and properly inflated, and slow down in heavy rain; hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and lights by:
options: a:Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.,b:Stopping immediately even if in an intersection.,c:Moving into the right lane and continuing slowly.
note: Pull to the right curb and stop, taking care not to block intersections, so emergency vehicles can pass.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must be prepared to produce:
options: a:Their license.,b:Proof of insurance only.,c:Proof of registration only.
note: When stopped, drivers are required to produce their driver license; they should also have proof of registration and insurance available.

question: What are “”no zones”” around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into the truck’s blind spots or are so close they restrict maneuvering.,b:Areas where cars have several car lengths of space behind the truck.,c:Areas where cars always have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: No zones are truck blind spots or zones where a smaller vehicle is so close it limits the truck driver’s ability to stop or maneuver, increasing crash risk.

question: The term 'No zone' refers to:
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A special reduced-speed zone.,c:An area where loud stereos are restricted.
note: 'No zone' denotes the large blind spots around commercial trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may disappear from view.

question: Reaction time is slower after which of the following?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol acts as a depressant, slowing reflexes and reaction time while impairing vision and judgment, which decreases driving ability.

question: A "No standing" sign means you may:
options: a:Stop briefly only to pick up or drop off passengers.,b:Park if the driver remains in the vehicle.,c:Never stop for any reason.
note: No standing areas allow temporary stops to load or unload passengers but not parking for longer periods.

question: Which surface tends to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:An intersection,b:A bridge,c:A tunnel
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air on both sides and often freeze before other road surfaces.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark the edges of a crosswalk. What is true?
options: a:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be yielded to by vehicles.,b:Vehicles always have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:No one has right-of-way in a crosswalk.,d:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles in marked crosswalks.
note: Crosswalk markings indicate where pedestrians should cross; drivers must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Drive through slowly and carefully.,c:Drive until the water looks too deep.
note: Do not attempt to drive through standing or flowing water—the depth and current can be deceptive and dangerous; find another way.

question: What helps you avoid having to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Looking far ahead and maintaining a safe following distance.,b:Honk to get drivers ahead to move faster.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Constantly weaving between lanes.
note: Keeping a safe following distance and looking ahead lets you react to hazards without needing sudden emergency stops.

question: How can drivers adjust their behavior to travel more safely in winter weather?
options: a:Increase their following distances.,b:Operate at slower speeds.,c:Stop and turn more gently.,d:All of the above.
note: In winter, reduce speed, make stops and turns more gently, and increase following distance to allow for longer stopping times.

question: If you see pedestrians close to the road where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop when pedestrians are near the roadway; yield as required and pass cautiously.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,b:Only when pedestrians are waving you on.,c:Only if the pedestrian is not distracted.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk; stop and allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

question: What is the only medically proven method to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Give your body time.,b:Breathe in fresh air.,c:Drink coffee.
note: Time is the only way to lower BAC. Remedies like coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed alcohol elimination.

question: While driving down a long or steep hill, what should you be especially alert to?
options: a:Check your mirrors for speeding traffic behind you.,b:Assume all traffic is maintaining a consistent speed.,c:Watch over your shoulder for traffic behind you.
note: Vehicles can gain speed going downhill; monitor mirrors for rapidly approaching traffic and be ready to adjust speed.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (driving with one hand, talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Follow their example more closely.,c:Attempt to pass immediately.
note: A distracted driver increases crash risk. Allow extra distance so you have room to react if they make sudden moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may proceed through the intersection if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go through the intersection after yielding to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection.

question: True or false: Solid pavement lines separating lanes indicate a no-passing zone.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Solid lines show areas where passing is unsafe and prohibited; dashed lines indicate passing is allowed when safe.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol impairs judgment required for safe driving.,b:If you are below the legal BAC limit, your driving is not impaired.,c:If you can walk a straight line, it is safe to drive.,d:Alcohol has no effect on nighttime driving.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, which is essential for making safe driving decisions; any amount of alcohol can impair driving ability.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Maintain steady speed and pass the pedestrian immediately.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move, then pass.,d:Drive onto the shoulder to pass the pedestrian.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe to do so.

question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: Your first response to decreased visibility should be to slow down and drive more cautiously to match conditions.

question: When backing your vehicle, what is the correct visual technique?
options: a:Look over your shoulder and out the rear window.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Put your head out the driver's side window.,d:Only use a backup camera and no visual checks.
note: Turn and look through the rear window while backing; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you ever allowed to drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No, you may not pass by driving off the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Yes, when there are two or more lanes in your travel direction.,d:Yes, when the shoulder is paved.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to pass by driving onto the shoulder; do not pass off the pavement.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:Warning or road hazard ahead.,b:Interstate route marker.,c:School crossing sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs used to alert drivers to hazards or special conditions ahead.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the desired space.,b:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels sharply to the right immediately.
note: After selecting a space, check traffic, signal, and stop parallel to the car ahead of the space before beginning the backing maneuver.

question: At a railroad crossing that lacks signals, what should you do as you approach?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop while checking for trains.,b:Always come to a full stop whether you see a train or not.,c:Assume crossings always have signals so no special action is needed.
note: Approach unprotected crossings with caution, slow down, look both ways, and stop if you see or hear a train.

question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated and more impaired.,b:More sober.,c:More coordinated.,d:Less likely to be detected.
note: Higher BAC means greater impairment of judgment, reaction, and coordination.

question: Which of these affects braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is influenced by vehicle speed, brake and tire condition, and road surface condition.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, which lights should drivers use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Fog lights only regardless of conditions.
note: Low beam headlights help improve visibility in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams cause reflection and glare.

question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle because of the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a motorcycle.,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a compact hatchback.,d:When following a bicycle on the shoulder.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are harder to see; allow extra space so you can stop safely if needed.

question: Drowsiness while driving, like alcohol or drugs, can:
options: a:Impair judgment, slow reactions, and reduce awareness.,b:Improve concentration.,c:Make you a better driver.,d:Have no impact on driving safety.
note: Lack of sleep decreases reaction time and impairs decision-making similar to intoxication.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:Through vibration and sound, they alert inattentive drivers that their vehicles have left the travel lane.,b:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a change in roadway.

question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
options: a:Increase the effects of both and make driving more dangerous.,b:Decrease the effects of both.,c:Help relieve your illness.,d:Have no effect on impairment.
note: Alcohol combined with certain drugs can amplify impairment and greatly increase danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:Because it is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b:It lets other road users know your intentions.,c:Because it is always unsafe to turn off a signal early.
note: Signaling gives drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians advance notice of your intended action, reducing the chance of conflicts.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed at normal speed.
note: Slow and be prepared to stop; always yield to a pedestrian who is blind or using a guide dog or cane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.,b:Unbuckle and get out immediately.,c:Get your paperwork out before the officer reaches your car.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer's instructions; only retrieve documents when requested.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until signals are withdrawn.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Slow and continue while watching for children.
note: You must come to a full stop for a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended stop arm until it moves or the signal is withdrawn.

question: What do round road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Upcoming railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round traffic signs are often used to warn drivers of an approaching railroad crossing; when you see them, use additional caution.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision caused by fatigue.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with mirrors; always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly in an emergency, what is the correct technique?
options: a:Firmly pump your brakes.,b:Hold down the brake pedal without releasing.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes can help you stop quickly while retaining steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is parking prohibited among these options?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is unlawful to park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes; when parallel parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Only vehicles turning left, not straight traffic.,c:No one in particular.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians crossing the path of the turn.

question: Who may park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Only vehicles displaying the proper disabled plates or placards may legally park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,b:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,c:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not expect you to move out to pass; give bicycles extra space and caution.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They always have different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to spot; drivers must be alert to avoid collisions.

question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,b:Always obey the traffic light instead of the officer.,c:Honk to get the officer's attention.
note: Police officers directing traffic take precedence over traffic signals; follow their instructions for safe flow.

question: When is turning or stopping most hazardous during rainy conditions?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:One half hour after it stops raining.
note: Road oil mixes with the first rain and creates very slippery conditions during the initial half hour of rainfall; use extra caution when stopping or turning then.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions and proceed.,b:Obey the red light instead of the officer.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.,d:Follow what the vehicle ahead of you does.
note: Police traffic directions override traffic signals; obey the officer's instructions.

question: On major highways you should:
options: a:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards.,b:Look at one point ahead to focus.,c:Drive the same speed regardless of conditions.
note: Remain alert and scan the roadway to avoid highway hypnosis and react to sudden hazards.

question: What type of signs use an orange background?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:General destination signs.
note: Orange signs are used specifically for construction and maintenance warnings; exercise extra caution in these areas.

question: If you have had several beers, how will the effects of alcohol be reduced?
options: a:By taking a cold shower.,b:By waiting several hours.,c:By drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol; it takes roughly an hour per standard drink for the body to metabolize alcohol.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Whenever it may help prevent a collision.,b:To express frustration with a slow driver.,c:To get other drivers moving in a traffic jam.,d:To greet friends on the roadside.
note: Use your horn to attract attention to prevent collisions, not as an expression of anger or impatience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Speed up and get through the intersection.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When driving past parked cars you should:
options: a:Be prepared for people or vehicles to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Honk to warn pedestrians, then pass quickly.,c:Assume others will yield to you.
note: Keep space from parked vehicles and be ready for someone or some vehicle to emerge unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order of arrival; if multiple arrive together, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing in which of these situations?
options: a:When directed to do so by a flagger.,b:Only when there is a stop sign.,c:Only if gates are present.
note: Stop when a flagger directs you, when a stop sign controls the crossing, or when flashing signals and gates are operating. Always obey posted warnings.

question: How close to a crosswalk may you not park?
options: a:15 feet,b:10 feet,c:Five feet
note: Parking is prohibited within 15 feet of a crosswalk in order to preserve visibility and pedestrian safety.

question: In traffic flowing 50–55 mph, how are you least likely to be involved in a crash?
options: a:Stay within the common speed range of the traffic.,b:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most vehicles.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most vehicles.
note: Adjust your speed to travel smoothly with other vehicles (within posted limits); inconsistent speeds increase crash risk.

question: When you become too drowsy to drive safely, the best action is to:
options: a:Open all windows and crank the A/C.,b:Drink a large energy drink and continue driving.,c:Exit the roadway and rest.
note: Fatigue impairs reactions and judgment; the safest option is to stop and rest before continuing.

question: The first driving ability impaired by alcohol is:
options: a:Judgment,b:Vision,c:Balance
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, which leads to risky driving choices.

question: Under-21 drivers can have their license suspended for driving with what blood alcohol level?
options: a:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.,d:Only if breath test confirms impairment.
note: Maine enforces a zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21: any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including license suspension.

question: After making an emergency roadside stop, is applying the parking brake optional?
options: a:False — you should set your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop.,b:True — the parking brake is not necessary.,c:Only apply it on hills.,d:Only use it if you plan to leave the vehicle.
note: Set the parking brake and turn on emergency flashers to alert other drivers when stopped on the roadside in an emergency.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Turn immediately.,d:Ignore it if no other cars are present.
note: An octagonal sign always means Stop; stop fully, yield as required, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force other drivers to make room by maintaining speed.
note: If a safe gap isn't available, slow on the ramp and wait until you can safely accelerate to match freeway traffic speed before merging.

question: If a traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light, it means:
options: a:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to go.
note: When a green arrow is displayed with a red light, you are permitted to move only in the arrow's direction if the way is clear.

question: Why must you use extra caution when you see a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They may be blind and need the right-of-way.,b:They are always police officers.,c:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. Yield the right-of-way, be prepared to stop, and proceed only when safe.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.,b:Toward the center of the roadway.,c:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,d:Down at your dashboard and speedometer.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough sight of the roadway to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic on the freeway is merging into your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.,b:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When conditions allow, make reasonable space to let merging vehicles enter the flow of traffic safely.

question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
options: a:Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: BAC is the measure of alcohol concentration in the bloodstream and determines impairment level.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever yielding will help prevent a collision.,b:Only at uncontrolled intersections.,c:Never, because it confuses other drivers.
note: Do not assume others will yield; give up your right-of-way when necessary to avoid crashes or hazardous situations.

question: What is ''highway hypnosis'' and what causes it?
options: a:A drowsy, inattentive state caused by staring at the roadway for long periods without scanning.,b:A condition prevented by frequent rest stops.,c:A result of getting too much sleep the night before driving.
note: ''Highway hypnosis'' occurs when drivers stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, increasing the risk of missing hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:
options: a:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,b:Reduce speed sharply before entering the ramp.,c:Maintain highway speed while on the ramp.
note: Do not slow abruptly on the travel lanes; wait until you are on the exit ramp to reduce speed safely.

question: What colors are used for signs that indicate the distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Red with white letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are green with white letters or symbols.

question: What must a driver do regarding pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and do everything to avoid striking them.,b:Ignore the pedestrian since they are wrong.,c:Stop only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,d:Flash headlights to make them move faster.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and take all precautions to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is crossing unlawfully.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection or any marked crosswalk or stop line.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,c:Slow down and proceed if the road looks clear.
note: A red light means stop at the marked stop line, before an intersection, or before entering a crosswalk; remain stopped until the light changes.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon,b:Square,c:Circle,d:Rectangle
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) shape is used exclusively for stop signs to make them easily recognizable.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid out of control, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Stay off the brakes.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes lightly.
note: If you skid, avoid braking; concentrate on steering to regain control, then once stable you can brake smoothly.

question: A stopped school bus ahead in your lane displays flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited the bus.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: Drivers must stop and remain stopped for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: On a road without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on:
options: a:The side facing oncoming traffic.,b:The side with the lightest traffic.,c:The same side as vehicle traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing traffic so they can see oncoming vehicles and react accordingly.

question: A lane-use control signal displaying a solid yellow X means what?
options: a:The lane signal is about to change to a red X; clear the lane.,b:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.,c:Drivers may use the lane only to make left turns.
note: A steady yellow X warns that the lane will soon close to your direction of travel; move out of the lane when safe.

question: Wearing both a lap belt and shoulder strap during a collision increases your chances of survival by three to four times. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Wearing both a lap belt and shoulder strap greatly increases survival chances compared with wearing no belt or only a lap belt.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through the flood.,b:Drive in the center of the roadway only.,c:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately in the water.,d:Proceed if the water looks shallow enough.
note: Never try to drive through flooded roads, as water depth and hidden hazards can be deceptive; turn around safely.

question: Road surfaces tend to freeze more quickly when they are:
options: a:In shaded areas (for example, under trees or buildings).,b:Flat open areas in full sun.,c:Curvy sections exposed to wind.,d:Recently repaved sections only.
note: Shaded roadway sections freeze earlier and stay icy longer than sunlit areas; use extra caution.

question: While driving in the rain, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in rainy conditions to improve visibility and reduce glare for yourself and other drivers.

question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a level roadside with no curb.
note: Turn wheels when parked on a slope so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

question: A distraction while driving is:
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Something that makes you pay more attention to driving.,c:Only things inside the car.
note: Any activity or object that draws attention away from driving is a distraction and can lead to collisions.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Whenever you notice a vehicle behind you.,c:After you begin moving the car.,d:Only during long trips.
note: Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat and mirrors so you can use them without leaning; do not wait until the car is moving.

question: Do yellow pavement markings indicate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Yellow pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white separates same-direction lanes.

question: When backing up, you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window over your right shoulder and back up slowly.,b:Rely solely on your rearview mirror.,c:Press the accelerator to move quickly.,d:Close your eyes and estimate distance.
note: Use direct vision by looking over your shoulder through the rear window and back up slowly at low speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must stop when instructed by a police officer and also at steady or flashing red traffic lights; always obey traffic control devices and officers.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Only half the lane width.,c:Use of the bicycle lane at all times.
note: Motorcycles have the same rights to full lane width as other vehicles and should be afforded room and respect.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two lanes move in your direction and you're in the left lane with faster drivers behind, you should:
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe so traffic can pass.,b:Stay in the left lane regardless of traffic behind you.,c:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.,d:Speed up to prevent others from passing on the right.
note: Use the right lane if you are driving slower than the flow of traffic to allow faster vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: There are situations when driving 10 mph might still be too fast. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must drive slower than the posted limit when conditions (traffic, weather, visibility) make higher speeds unsafe.

question: If you are already within an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop.,c:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear it safely rather than stopping abruptly.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by improving communication with other road users?
options: a:Use signals, headlights, horn, and other appropriate warnings to communicate.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: Communicate intentions through signal use, brake lights, horn, and lane position to reduce surprises and conflicts.

question: A large truck turning right onto a multi-lane street may:
options: a:Need to swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:Always stay strictly in the right lane while turning.,c:Complete the turn in either of the two right lanes without swinging wide.
note: Long vehicles often need to swing wide when turning right because their rear wheels track a shorter path than the front.

question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can kill.,b:Driving too slowly is always safe.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are skilled.
note: Higher speeds increase the likelihood and severity of crashes; speeding is a leading cause of fatalities.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow mean to drivers?
options: a:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is imminent.,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction immediately.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected signal is ending and a red arrow will follow; stop if you can do so safely.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may attempt risky passes.,b:Appropriate if you are unsure of the posted limit.,c:Recommended anytime weather is bad.
note: Driving significantly slower than traffic flow can create dangerous passing maneuvers and increase crash risk.

question: Who must wear a seat belt in a motor vehicle?
options: a:Passengers under 18 years of age and the driver.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only adult passengers.
note: All occupants required to be restrained by federal vehicle regulations (including passengers under 18 and drivers) must wear seat belts.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red, what should you do?
options: a:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
note: Yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when you have a green light; allow them to cross safely.

question: Does using a cell phone to talk or text while driving significantly increase your crash risk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Using a phone while driving distracts your eyes, hands, and mind and increases the likelihood of a collision.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Make eye contact then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should stop to allow them to cross safely.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They require a longer distance to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than cars.,c:All large trucks stop quickly because of air brakes.,d:They always stop within the same distance as cars at the same speed.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed.

question: Alcohol consumption impairs which of the following driver abilities?
options: a:Judgement.,b:Perception.,c:Emotional control.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, perception, and emotional control—abilities critical for safe driving. (All listed areas are affected.)

question: What best ensures safety when you are backing your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for obstacles before getting in and backing up.,b:Check only your rearview mirrors after getting in.,c:Honk your horn immediately before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, exit and check behind the vehicle for children, small objects, or other hazards; use mirrors and cameras as additional aids.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They require less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots and need extra space and distance to steer and stop safely; avoid lingering beside them.

question: If someone behind you is driving aggressively, you should:
options: a:Get out of their way and avoid eye contact.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: Move over or slow safely to let an aggressive driver pass and avoid escalating the situation.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and allow them to pass.,b:Retaliate by tailgating.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: Keep calm, avoid engagement, and yield to aggressive drivers to increase distance and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a business or residential area?
options: a:25 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:35 mph.,d:30 mph.
note: In Maine, the standard speed limit in business or residential districts is 25 mph unless posted otherwise.

question: When is the proper time to adjust your mirrors?
options: a:Before starting the engine.,b:While backing out of your driveway.,c:Only when approaching highway speeds.,d:After you begin driving.
note: Before you start driving, adjust mirrors so you can use them without leaning; you won't have time to adjust them in heavy traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers who arrived before you have the right-of-way.,b:The driver who signals first always has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the left always has the right-of-way.
note: At multi-way stops, yield to drivers who arrived before you; proceed in turn when it is safe to do so.

question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe.,b:Drivers may not pass at any time.,c:Both lanes travel in the same direction.
note: A single broken yellow centerline means passing is permitted for either direction when safe.

question: Which light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A steady yellow light.,d:A steady green arrow.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and proceed with caution; it does not require a stop.

question: Which of these can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, medications or illicit drugs, and lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol and not prescription medication.,d:None of the above.
note: Driving ability is impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, you should signal:
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling toward a curb and when re-entering traffic so other road users know your intentions.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before operating your vehicle.,b:Loudly play music so you won't think about it while driving.,c:Drive quickly on the highway to let off steam.,d:Begin driving immediately to get home sooner.
note: Strong emotions affect judgment; calm down before driving to maintain safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Slow down and cross carefully.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Proceed without slowing down.
note: A flashing yellow means exercise caution: slow down, look, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right; proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what actions should you take to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Check the inside rearview mirror only.,c:Slow down before changing lanes.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to confirm the lane is clear of vehicles and motorcycles hidden in blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the interstate and merge when safe.,b:Force their way because they are entering traffic.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp before merging.,d:Expect drivers to change lanes for them.
note: Yield to traffic on the interstate and accelerate to merge safely with the flow of traffic.

question: How should you prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead?
options: a:Continually scan the entire road and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at a single point.,c:Drive with your foot resting on the brake at all times.,d:Only look as you approach intersections.
note: Search the road ahead and the sides to identify potential hazards early and be prepared to react.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn out, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Bad suspension reduces vehicle stability and control, making it harder to handle bumps and turns safely.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: For best protection wear both the lap and shoulder belts. Using only one part significantly reduces effectiveness.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and apply the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator and slow gradually; avoid hard braking until the vehicle has slowed.

question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,b:Assuming the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,c:Assuming they will let you pass if you signal.
note: Do not rely on other drivers to create space; ensure there is enough room to pass and return safely before beginning.

question: Does a driver need to allow as much following distance when behind a motorcycle as behind a car?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers should allow at least three to four seconds behind motorcycles since they can stop quickly and maneuver.

question: If you encounter a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield to vehicles.,c:Honk to alert the pedestrian of your presence.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is blind or visually impaired; you must yield and take care to avoid endangering them.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle using high beams that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,c:Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
note: If an oncoming vehicle's high beams are blinding you, glance toward the right edge of the road and use lane markings to stay on course until it passes.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:You must not pass other vehicles.,b:Reduce your speed immediately.,c:A traffic light is ahead.,d:You may pass if no oncoming traffic is visible.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates a no-passing zone for your direction.

question: What must you do when you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.,b:Stop immediately where you are and turn off the engine.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If safe, pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop to create a clear path for the emergency vehicle; in heavy traffic keep moving slowly until you can safely pull over.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Flash your headlights and retaliate.,c:Attempt to speed up and race them.
note: Avoid escalating the situation; get out of the way and let the aggressive driver pass.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Make abrupt turns to clear water quickly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to test grip.
note: Lower your speed on wet roads to reduce hydroplaning risk and maintain good tire traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, at what speed should you be traveling?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit only, regardless of traffic speed.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic so you can merge smoothly and safely.

question: Which behavior best describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.,b:Keeping eyes on the road while adjusting radio.,c:Watching the vehicle directly in front only.,d:Frequently checking mirrors and surroundings.
note: Do not be distracted by passengers, maps, or daydreaming. Continuously scan the road and mirrors to stay attentive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How are fines for moving violations in school zones typically different?
options: a:Fines are doubled in school zones.,b:Fines are reduced in school zones.,c:Fines are unchanged in school zones.,d:Fines are waived during school hours.
note: In Maine, fines for moving traffic violations are doubled within school zones; exercise extra caution when driving through them.

question: Why should you avoid making a sudden stop in front of a large truck or bus?
options: a:Because large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,b:Because large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds.,c:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their rearview mirrors.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; a sudden stop in front of them can result in the large vehicle being unable to stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver whose left arm and hand are extended downward is signaling what?
options: a:Stop or slow down.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: With the left arm extended downward, the driver is signaling that they intend to slow down or stop.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using its siren and/or flashing lights, what must a driver do?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right and turn on their vehicle's four-way flashers.
note: You must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop to allow an emergency vehicle using lights or sirens to pass.

question: What headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Turn off the ignition.
note: If you begin to skid, release the accelerator or brake to regain balance and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: What should you do first before stopping your vehicle at a signal or sign?
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before stopping, check your mirrors to be aware of traffic behind and around you so you can stop smoothly and safely.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Children have less developed reflexes and are harder to see, so extra space is needed.,b:Children always follow the rules perfectly.,c:They are larger and easier to see than adults.,d:Children can stop more quickly than adults.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see, especially near schools and parks, so give them extra room and caution.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally do what?
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than passenger vehicles do.
note: Due to size and weight, trucks need more room to stop and maneuver; give them extra clearance.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, reduce speed gradually, and pull off the road.,b:Slam on your brakes immediately.,c:Keep driving at the same speed and try to get to a service area.
note: Grip the wheel firmly to maintain control, ease off the accelerator, and carefully slow and steer to a safe place off the roadway before stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders simultaneously.
note: When changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and look over the shoulder on the side you plan to move to in order to check the blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver begins to pass you, how can you help them re-enter your lane?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Signal the other driver aggressively to speed up.
note: When someone is passing, maintain or slightly adjust speed to create a safe space for them to merge back in front of you.

question: Is it lawful to share a lane side-by-side with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A motorcycle needs a full lane to maneuver safely; you must not drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, you should look for a gap of how many seconds?
options: a:Four seconds,b:One to two seconds,c:Three seconds
note: Identify about a four-second gap in traffic so you and the car behind have safe following distance when you merge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass:
options: a:On a hill or curve, at an intersection, or when a school bus's lights are flashing.,b:Only when a police officer is present.,c:Whenever a car in front is driving under the speed limit.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: Never pass where you cannot see ahead (hills/curves), at intersections, or when a stopped school bus is loading/unloading with flashing red lights.

question: What is the correct general action when roads are slippery?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive the posted speed with caution.,c:Drive more quickly.
note: Reduce your speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or ice; you may need to drive well below the posted speed limit.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You always have the right-of-way at railroad crossings.,c:Use cruise control to maintain speed over tracks.
note: If a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal directs you to stop at a railroad crossing, you must do so. Use caution near tracks.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction because of water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Apply firm braking immediately.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,c:Accelerate to regain traction.
note: If you begin to hydroplane, gradually ease off the accelerator and don't apply the brakes. Allow the vehicle to slow until tires regain contact.

question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Stop at the curb before crossing.,b:Always know when it is safe to cross.,c:Possibly run into the street without looking.
note: Children may not recognize traffic risks and could dart into the road unexpectedly; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and details of the accident.,b:Have done as much as you can and leave.,c:Must stay until the police arrive regardless of circumstances.
note: If you cannot find the owner, leave a note with your contact information and details of the incident, and report it as required by law.

question: What must you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield to others as needed, and proceed when safe.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which of the following?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.,d:All of the above.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so, if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

question: Which action can help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently to warn others.,c:Text or talk on your phone to stay calm.
note: Signaling intentions, obeying traffic rules, and driving courteously all help reduce road rage incidents.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same as a stop sign; come to a full stop before proceeding.,b:The traffic signal is broken and can be ignored.,c:You do not have to stop if the way is clear.
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop and yielding to appropriate traffic and pedestrians, similar to a stop sign.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child even in a low-speed collision.,c:You should always make sure all passengers are using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint.
note: Always buckle up and ensure children are properly restrained in the rear seat per safety guidelines; rear-facing infant restraints should not be used in front of an active airbag.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if it can be done safely and without interfering with other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss the exit you wanted to take off a freeway, you should:
options: a:Go on to the next exit.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back to the exit.,c:Cross the median and turn around.
note: Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a freeway; use the next exit to safely change direction.

question: When you approach a heavy truck from behind on an uphill, you should be aware that:
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You can always safely pass the truck on the hill.,c:It is legal to pass on a hill with limited visibility.
note: Large vehicles often travel more slowly uphill; on hills with limited visibility it can be unsafe and unlawful to pass.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be prepared to stop.,b:Always speed up to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Ignore gates and proceed if no train is visible.
note: Slow, look and be ready to stop. If signals are active or gates are down, stop 15–50 feet before the tracks.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal tells you to:
options: a:Stop before proceeding.,b:Drive with caution.,c:Yield to oncoming traffic only.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to proceed with caution but does not require a full stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Yellow centerlines on the road separate what type of traffic?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads and separate opposing directions of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a likely result of driving much slower than the speed limit?
options: a:Is a very safe driver.,b:Always has the right-of-way.,c:May create a hazard and you may need to let others pass.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can be dangerous; if your slow speed causes backup, you should pull off when safe and let others pass.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.,b:Accelerating quickly at each green light.,c:Idling in your driveway with the engine running.,d:Constantly switching between gears.
note: Avoid rapid acceleration and unnecessary braking; scanning ahead and slowing gradually improves fuel economy.

question: If there are two adjacent railroad tracks, what must you do after one train passes?
options: a:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
note: When multiple tracks exist, another train may be approaching on the adjacent track; wait until you are sure all tracks are clear.

question: On which side(s) of your vehicle should you maintain a space cushion?
options: a:Only to the front of the vehicle,b:Only to the back of the vehicle,c:Only to the left and right of the vehicle
note: Maintain a space cushion all around your vehicle—front, back, left, and right—to give yourself room to react to hazards.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Speed up because a lane ends ahead.
note: Work zone signs indicate possible workers, equipment, or lane closures; slow down and follow directions.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:
