options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself against the seatback.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not unbuckle; brace yourself and press your head into the head restraint to reduce whiplash risk.

question: On long trips, preventing drowsiness is achieved by:
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for rest and stretching.,b:Turning the radio on loudly.,c:Slowing down to conserve energy.
note: Regular stops for rest and stretching help prevent drowsiness on long drives.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before entering a curve or intersection?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
note: Slow down before entering curves and intersections; braking while turning can cause a skid.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear.,b:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.,c:Drive through without stopping if no other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light means stop (like a stop sign). Stop, yield as required, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to let them know you’re there.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Yield to allow safe re-entry.
note: When a transit vehicle signals it is re-entering traffic after loading/unloading, you must yield by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping to let it merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any other traffic with the right-of-way.,b:Maintain your normal speed and complete the turn.,c:Stop before turning even if no one is present.,d:Turn without checking for pedestrians if the light is green.
note: On a green light you may turn, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic lawfully in the intersection.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually without braking hard.,b:Press the brake pedal as hard as possible immediately.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: Keep control, release the accelerator, and allow the vehicle to slow before braking gently and pulling over safely.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (like a truck with blind spots),b:Only when following a small passenger car.,c:When behind a compact sedan.,d:Never; following distance is constant.
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles that have limited rear visibility and can block your view of the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a suggested safe speed.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
note: Speed limits represent the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; slow down for poor conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what steps should you take to merge safely?
options: a:Use your mirrors and check blind spots; use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed; yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already in the travel lane before merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red signal, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and pass through if clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.,d:Proceed as if the signal were a flashing yellow.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when clear.

question: If you approach an accident scene, when should you stop?
options: a:Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Always stop to look, even if you are not involved.,c:Keep moving and ignore the scene completely.,d:Park nearby and take photos.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; otherwise keep moving and stay focused on driving.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Highway signs that warn of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions; obey them for safety.

question: Drivers should be most alert for deer and moose at what times?
options: a:At dusk and dawn.,b:Only during the night.,c:Only at midday.
note: Wildlife, including deer and moose, are most active around dawn and dusk; be extra cautious at those times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and lights, it:
options: a:Has the right-of-way and you must yield to it.,b:Has no different rights than other traffic.,c:Should be followed closely by other vehicles.
note: Yield to police, fire, and ambulance vehicles using sirens or flashing lights; obey instructions from their loudspeaker.

question: Under low visibility due to fog, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to see farther.,c:Increase your speed to get out of the fog quickly.
note: In fog, slow down, use low beams (not high beams), and, if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely until conditions improve.

question: When driving in dense fog, which of these is correct?
options: a:Use low beam headlights and drive cautiously at reduced speeds.,b:Use high beam headlights to see farther.,c:Keep your normal speed to avoid causing delays.
note: In fog, use low beams (not high beams) and slow down; if visibility is extremely poor, safely pull off the roadway.

question: Regarding curves, the most important rule is to:
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part, then brake.,c:Accelerate through the curve for better traction.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve so your vehicle's inertia doesn't carry you too wide.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: Slow down before entering a curve to help maintain control and avoid excessive lateral force.

question: How often must motor vehicles bearing a Maine registration be inspected?
options: a:Once a year.,b:Once every two years.,c:Once every four years.
note: In Maine, registered motor vehicles must be inspected at an official inspection station once a year before being operated on public roadways.

question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach their destination faster.
note: In adverse weather, increase spacing between vehicles to allow for longer stopping distances.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you have lost control of your vehicle or to avoid a collision.,b:To express frustration at another driver.,c:When passing another car on the highway.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of danger or to avoid a crash; do not use it to express anger or frustration.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that greatly increases crash risk.,b:Very uncommon and not a major concern.,c:Always acceptable if you are an experienced driver.,d:Only an issue for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving significantly raises crash risk for drivers, passengers, and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to emergency vehicles when:
options: a:You see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:Only when other vehicles yield.
note: Yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left; if struck from behind, this prevents being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When can you legally go around or under a railroad crossing gate that is lowered?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can clearly see in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Never drive around or under any lowered gate at a railroad crossing; wait until the gate is fully raised and lights have stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:It is a two-way road where passing is allowed when safe.,b:It is a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair and temporary markings apply.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposite-direction traffic and allow passing when it is safe to do so.

question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: Remove your foot from the throttle to slow gradually; if more deceleration is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Slowly pass stopped vehicles without checking.,c:Only look straight ahead.,d:Ignore pedestrians if you have the right-of-way.
note: Whenever people or other traffic might enter your path, look left and right to ensure nothing is coming before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane on the right.,b:Whenever there is space on the right shoulder to pass.,c:On a narrow bridge if traffic is slow.
note: You may pass on the right when there is an available passing lane or when a vehicle ahead is waiting or signaling to turn left. You may not pass by driving off the pavement or on a narrow bridge.

question: If a driver accumulates how many points in one year will their license be suspended?
options: a:12 points,b:18 points,c:20 points
note: In Maine, accumulating 12 or more points within a 12-month period can result in a license suspension.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.
note: Alcohol impairs alertness, slows reflexes, and distorts perception of speed and distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should do which of the following?
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors, then glance over your shoulder for blind spots.,b:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,c:Only check your side view mirror.,d:Only rely on a backup camera.
note: Check mirrors for traffic and look over your shoulder just before moving to account for blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should:
options: a:See the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Wait until you can see the whole front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, and check blind spots, before merging back.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Let go of the steering wheel.,b:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Be ready to apply the brakes.
note: Do not let go of the steering wheel; brace against the seat and head restraint and be prepared to brake to avoid being pushed into another vehicle.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings and signs?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only found in construction zones.,c:They provide information and guidance for drivers.
note: Pavement markings and signs help drivers position vehicles, inform about passing zones, warn of hazards, and provide other vital information.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag.,c:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots on each side; avoid driving alongside them for extended periods so the driver can see you.

question: Are drivers required to yield to children playing in the streets?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Exercise extreme caution around children; slow down in residential areas, near playgrounds, and in school zones.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Apply your brakes and then resume original speed.,b:Speed up to increase distance.,c:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.
note: If you cannot safely change lanes, slowly reduce speed when safe; this often encourages the driver behind to pass and reduces collision risk.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (to the right).,b:Straight ahead.,c:Toward the center of the road (left).
note: Without a curb, turn wheels so the vehicle would roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure safe driving afterwards?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving to sober up.,c:Take a cold shower, then drive.,d:Wait 10 minutes and then drive if you feel fine.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving while impaired; coffee or showers don't lower BAC.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, you should pull to the right-hand edge and wait for it to pass. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When an emergency vehicle uses warning devices, you must immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What should you do when it begins to rain while you are driving?
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down.
note: Heavy rain reduces visibility and road traction—slow down, use headlights, and pull over if visibility becomes unsafe.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is NOT affected by which of the following?
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks; the beverage type does not determine BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to turn left at the upcoming corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:All approaching vehicles.,b:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a Walk signal.
note: When making a left turn you must yield to all appropriate road users, including pedestrians and oncoming traffic with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the ramp end and wait for a large gap.,c:Slow down significantly to avoid merging conflicts.
note: Use the acceleration lane to increase to the speed of traffic, signal, look for an opening, and merge smoothly when safe.

question: As your speed increases, what must you do to stay safe?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance, so scan far ahead to recognize hazards and allow more time to react.

question: Is it acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates under any circumstances?
options: a:No — under no circumstances should you drive around a lowered gate.,b:Yes — if the train has passed recently.,c:Only when flashing lights have stopped.,d:When directed by another driver.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings with active warnings and never attempt to go around lowered gates or barriers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign—you must stop and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:Stop only if other cars are present.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to others, then proceeding when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: Drivers must stop when approaching an intersection if their view is obscured and inch forward only until a clear view in both directions is obtained.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to begin a pass in a passing zone if you cannot complete it before the zone ends?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You may not start a pass if you cannot finish it before reaching a no-passing zone; it is unsafe to be mid-pass when the zone ends.

question: When should you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If there isn’t room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.,b:Only in cities with frequent trains.,c:Only if you are transporting two or more young children.
note: Always ensure there is room to completely clear the tracks before crossing; never stop on the tracks or where you would be trapped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: Driving slowly enough to impede normal traffic flow can be illegal and may result in a citation.

question: Which of the following may be used on some highways to guide drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Arrows and lane-control signals such as flashing yellow arrow indicators.,b:White lines on the side of the road only.,c:Flashing red lights only.
note: Arrows or lane control signals (including arrow indicators) are used to show which lanes are designated for turns or through movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but an officer signals for you to stop, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer's directions and stop.,b:Follow the green light instead of the officer.,c:Follow what the vehicle ahead does.,d:Slow and then proceed if clear.
note: Police directions override traffic signals; follow the officer's instructions.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect what aspects of a driver?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment, reaction time, and coordination and can affect driving ability.

question: Is alcohol a major factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Alcohol is a leading cause of fatal crashes; it impairs vision, reaction time, judgment, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a steady red light, drivers should:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped, unless turning right where allowed.,b:Drive through if no cross traffic is visible.,c:Only stop if a police officer is present.
note: A steady red light requires stopping; right turns on red are allowed only where not prohibited and after yielding.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane when safe.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake very hard and sharply steer to the right.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually; avoid panic braking and steer smoothly to pull off safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination — all critical driving skills.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only when involved in a collision.,b:Whenever stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,c:Only when stopped and cited.
note: You must carry evidence of financial responsibility and show proof of insurance and your license to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right lane immediately.,d:Wait for a police officer to direct traffic.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop, yielding to others, and proceeding only when it is safe.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic before turning.,b:You do not need to yield when turning.,c:Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.,d:The turn is protected and you may proceed without caution.
note: A solid yellow arrow indicates the green arrow protection is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you.,c:Never yield under any circumstances.,d:Turn immediately when the signal changes regardless of oncoming traffic.
note: Left turns require yielding to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before turning.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; a solid line indicates passing is not allowed.

question: Road rage and aggressive driving may be reduced by:
options: a:Allowing extra travel time and obeying speed limits.,b:Refusing to signal.,c:Driving faster than other vehicles to get ahead.
note: Allow extra time, obey speed limits, and use signals to decrease frustration and reduce aggressive driving incidents.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, it is a good idea to:
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Drive with one eye open at a time.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—to rest, stretch, and refresh to avoid drowsiness while driving long distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly if you misjudged timing.
note: Even on green, yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection before proceeding.

question: Are posters, signs, or window decals on vehicle windows permitted?
options: a:They are prohibited unless specifically required by law.,b:They are a fun way to personalize your car.,c:Allowed if they only slightly obstruct visibility.
note: Window obstructions are prohibited unless the item is specifically required by law. Do not place signs or stickers that block visibility.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has its red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red flashers and a stop arm extended, you must stop until the lights stop flashing and the arm is retracted.

question: Where should you allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped?
options: a:When stopped on an uphill slope.,b:At a stop sign in a flat area.,c:At a traffic circle.,d:On a straight, level road.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope in case the vehicle in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but opposing traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,b:Accelerate quickly once the first lane is clear.,c:Rely on an oncoming driver to wave you through.
note: Only begin a multi-lane left turn when you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and it's safe to proceed.

question: When weather changes suddenly, what should you do?
options: a:Adjust your driving to the new conditions, including slowing in rain or fog.,b:Maintain your previous speed regardless of conditions.,c:Ignore vehicles behind you since they should adapt.,d:Only worry about weather when it snows heavily.
note: Sudden weather requires changes in driving—reduce speed in rain or fog and be aware of others.

question: You should remove snow, frost, and ice from which parts of your vehicle before driving?
options: a:All windows, headlights, and taillights.,b:Only the windshield.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear visibility is essential for safe driving. Remove snow and ice from all windows and lights so you can see and be seen.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside, what must you do if safe to do so?
options: a:Change lanes to give the stopped vehicle extra space and slow down.,b:Continue in your lane at the posted speed.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
note: Move over a lane away from stopped emergency, roadside assistance, or tow vehicles when it is safe; otherwise slow to below the posted speed limit and proceed with caution.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Has no effect on driving.,b:Nearly doubles the risk of being in a fatal crash.,c:Only affects very inexperienced drivers.
note: Even small increases in BAC can substantially increase crash risk; each 0.02% rise nearly doubles the chance of a fatal crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road at the first safe opportunity to let traffic pass.,b:Keep driving at the same speed until a passing zone appears.,c:Increase your speed abruptly to clear the backup.,d:Stay in lane and prevent others from passing.
note: If you're impeding traffic on a two-lane road, pull over safely and let faster vehicles pass.

question: Does an octagonal sign always require drivers to stop?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A red octagonal sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and be entirely in the left lane while passing.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.,c:Stay as far right as possible because the motorcycle is small.
note: When passing a motorcycle, give the rider a full lane width and do not share the lane; position your vehicle fully in the adjacent lane to pass safely.

question: Before entering an intersection, what order should you scan traffic?
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Look left, then right, then left again before proceeding; vehicles from the left will be closer and can present more immediate risk.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, you should first:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately and sharply.,c:Stop where you are and remain in the vehicle.
note: If you run off the pavement, slow down, check traffic, and gently steer back onto the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Ensure the passing lane is clear.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Ignore other traffic's speed.
note: Make sure the lane you intend to use for passing is clear and signal before changing lanes.

question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians in the street even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly?
options: a:Yes — drivers must yield and take steps to avoid hitting them.,b:No — only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian follows signals.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway and take actions to avoid collisions, even if the pedestrian is careless.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians who use guide dogs or white canes must always be given the right-of-way.

question: What does a red arrow displayed on a traffic signal instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,b:Slow and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Stop then proceed when clear, even if the signal stays red.
note: A red arrow requires a full stop and drivers must not turn in that direction until a green light or green arrow appears (unless posted otherwise).

question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:
options: a:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid frightening it.,b:Sound your horn and speed past.,c:Take no special action.
note: Approach animals carefully and pass slowly to prevent startling them and causing unpredictable movement.

question: Which types of drugs may affect your ability to drive safely?
options: a:Illegal drugs only.,b:Only prescription medications.,c:Legal prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can all impair driving.
note: Many types of drugs—illegal, prescription, and OTC—can impair driving ability; always know a drug's side effects before driving.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and may be illegal.,b:Yes, it is always a good defensive technique.,c:Yes, it is safer than driving faster than others.
note: While reducing speed in hazardous conditions is appropriate, driving excessively slowly and impeding traffic can be unsafe and may violate the law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit, leave, and return to the proper exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder to reach the exit.
note: Do not back up on the travel lane or shoulder; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your intended route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either direction across which centerline marking?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow centerline.,b:Single broken yellow centerline.,c:Double solid yellow centerline.
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-way road means passing is prohibited for traffic from either direction.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be alert for cross traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds have passed.,c:You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:You have finished signaling for at least one second.
note: Return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle often mounted on the rear of farm equipment and slow vehicles traveling 25 mph or less.

question: If your turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use hand signals.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Use your horn.
note: When turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to show other drivers your intended turn.

question: Driving while impaired by medication is:
options: a:Never permitted.,b:Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Allowed if prescribed by a doctor.
note: Driving under the influence of any substance that impairs ability is illegal and unsafe.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a:There are less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead and to use caution.,b:It is summer and conditions are normal.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn drivers of highway work and potential hazards; slow down and drive carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:You only follow them if other traffic is present.,d:They apply only during daylight.
note: Traffic control devices direct and inform drivers and must be obeyed at all times.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Drive with your four-way flashers on.
note: You must turn on your headlights at dusk or in poor visibility; use low beams when near other vehicles.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake lightly.
note: Braking suddenly during a skid can worsen it; focus on steering to regain control and then brake smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, what should entering drivers do?
options: a:Enter and keep right of other traffic.,b:Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.,c:Drive clockwise around the central island.
note: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise; entering drivers must yield to traffic already in the circle and follow signs and lane markings.

question: If you stop along the roadway at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on.,b:Turn off all your lights.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: At night, activate emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on so other road users can see your vehicle.

question: It is unlawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; cars must not try to occupy the same lane space as a motorcycle.

question: Is it safe to stop on a railroad track if you are moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks; ensure there is room to clear the tracks before you begin to cross.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving are likely to:
options: a:Make no driving errors.,b:Have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle.,c:Be better drivers because they are not hungry.
note: Eating and drinking distract drivers by requiring hand and eye movement away from driving tasks, increasing accident risk.

question: When you see a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line in the center of the road, what does that mean?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass; those next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.,d:Lanes move in opposite directions and neither may pass.
note: A broken yellow beside a solid yellow means passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line.

question: Is it ever legal to drive through, around, or under a lowered railroad gate or barrier?
options: a:False — never drive through or under a lowered gate.,b:True — if the train has passed.,c:Only if directed by a railroad employee.,d:Only at night when visibility is reduced.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to go around or under lowered railroad gates; always stop and wait until they are raised.

question: How should a lap belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Snugly across your hip bones and the lower abdomen.,b:Loose and comfortable across your stomach.,c:Hidden under the seat cushion.,d:Crossing only the upper chest.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should rest comfortably across the chest.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches?
options: a:Try to reach your destination before it catches up.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right and stopping if safe; if in an intersection, clear it before pulling over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into your lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as you clear the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:After you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough room.

question: If a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through.,c:Stop immediately regardless of distance.
note: A solid yellow light warns the signal will soon turn red; stop before entering if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: To check blind spots and see vehicles not visible in mirrors, you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulders.,b:Check only inside rearview mirror.,c:Check only outside mirrors.
note: Blind spots are outside mirror coverage areas; a quick shoulder check is necessary before lane changes.

question: You must obey directions from a flagger in a construction zone.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Flaggers direct traffic in work zones; failing to obey them is illegal and unsafe.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window every few seconds.,c:Rely solely on the side mirrors.,d:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots by tailgating.
note: Check your rearview mirror often to monitor traffic behind you and adjust your driving as needed.

question: True or False: Roads are most dangerous at the start of a light rain when oils mix with water.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Roads can be especially slippery at the start of light rain as oils on the pavement mix with water, forming a greasy surface.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historical sites?
options: a:Brown.,b:Red.,c:Orange.,d:Blue.
note: Brown signs are used to indicate cultural, historical, and recreational sites.

question: Is failing an alcohol test the only way to be convicted of an OUI?
options: a:False — you can be convicted even if you refuse testing or based on officer testimony.,b:True — conviction requires a failed test.,c:Only if there is a breath test result.,d:Only if there is DNA evidence.
note: You can be convicted of Operating Under the Influence even without test results; refusal or officer observations can lead to conviction.

question: If you plan to slow where other drivers may not expect it, what should you do before slowing?
options: a:Quickly tap your brakes three or four times to alert drivers behind you.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Release the accelerator and drift to a stop.
note: Give a quick tap of the brakes to illuminate your brake lights and alert drivers behind you before slowing unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic if needed.
note: Drivers entering from private roads must yield to traffic and pedestrians on the public road.

question: What do downward-facing triangular signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Yield.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-facing triangular sign is typically a yield sign, indicating you must yield to other traffic or pedestrians as necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline beside your lane indicates you may cross the centerline to pass if it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone or where a sign prohibits it.,b:Passing only over a railroad crossing.,c:Passing when the centerline is broken and it's safe.,d:Passing when there is no oncoming traffic regardless of markings.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no-passing zones, at rail crossings, on hills/curves where you can't see, and where signs prohibit passing.

question: What blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of a car.
note: Rubbernecking causes congestion and secondary collisions; keep moving unless required to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,c:Roll down your window and ask another driver for directions.
note: Do not back up or make a U-turn on the highway. Continue to the next exit and safely return to your intended location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Attempt to change lanes while in an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal your move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you legally follow an emergency vehicle that is using its alarm?
options: a:500 feet,b:1,000 feet,c:One mile
note: It is unlawful to follow an emergency vehicle that is responding to an emergency closer than 500 feet; give them room to operate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the maximum posted speed limit only under which conditions?
options: a:Under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The maximum posted speed limit is intended for ideal driving conditions; reduce speed when weather, traffic, or road conditions warrant.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Hazard (four-way) flashers.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams can reflect off the moisture and reduce visibility further.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn to warn children.
note: Pentagonal school signs indicate children may be present; be alert and ready to stop if needed.

question: If your vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: Vehicles equipped with ABS require firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal; ABS pumps the brakes automatically faster than you could.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should:
options: a:Park with all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway, if possible.,b:Stop in the right travel lane and leave hazard lights off.,c:Leave your vehicle where it stopped and stand in traffic to warn others.
note: If possible, move your vehicle completely off the main road, turn on hazards, and use other warning devices; remain in a safe place.

question: Is it safe to drive beside a large truck inside a roundabout?
options: a:False — you should not attempt to drive next to a large truck in a roundabout.,b:True — it's fine as long as you signal.,c:Only if the truck is turning left.,d:Only at speeds below 10 mph.
note: Large trucks may use more than one lane in a roundabout; do not try to drive next to them while they maneuver.

question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.
note: Always signal and check your mirrors, then glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before any lane change or pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop well back of the gates and wait until they lift.,b:Drive around the gates if you can't see a train.,c:Slow and drive around the gates cautiously.
note: You must stop for lowered gates and flashing signals and may not drive around them until it is safe and the gates are raised.

question: Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:35 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.,d:25 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around 35 mph depending on water depth and tire condition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign.,c:Use of your turn signals.
note: Space needed to cross traffic varies with road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and vehicles to your right and left arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: When multiple vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When a red light is showing but a green arrow points in the direction you want to go, when may you proceed?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:After first coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after the main light changes from red.
note: A green arrow indicates you may proceed in the arrow's direction if you are in the correct lane and yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up to assert yourself.
note: Avoid competing with aggressive drivers; safely move out of their path to reduce the chance of escalation and collisions.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Drive carefully, avoid slowing to stare, and obey posted directions.,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Decrease following distance to move through faster.,d:Pass without changing speed if you think it's safe.
note: Do not 'rubberneck' in work zones; drive carefully and follow traffic controls to maintain flow and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, you should:
options: a:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,b:Stop immediately anywhere you are, even in an intersection.,c:Continue driving slowly and let it pass.
note: Move to the right and stop safely, ensuring you do not obstruct intersections, to let emergency vehicles pass.

question: If you exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do before entering the curve?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: Reduce speed before entering the ramp curve; braking during a curve can lead to loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the right curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the left curb.
note: When turning, start from the lane closest to the direction you want to go; from a one-way street a left turn is made from the lane nearest the left curb.

question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?
options: a:Drivers cannot see as well at night, reducing visibility.,b:Traffic is always faster at night.,c:Road rules change after dark.,d:There are more pedestrians at night.
note: From one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise (or when visibility is less than 500 feet) you must use headlights because visibility is reduced.

question: Alcohol consumption negatively affects which abilities?
options: a:Alertness,b:Coordination and reaction time,c:All of the above
note: Alcohol impairs alertness, coordination, and reaction time, increasing crash risk and reducing control.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Accelerate rapidly out of turns.
note: Reduce speed and take turns more slowly than under normal conditions to maintain traction and control.

question: An aggressive driver may be identified by:
options: a:Erratic or improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the car.,c:Driving consistently below the speed limit.
note: Erratic lane changes, tailgating, or other hostile behaviors often indicate an aggressive driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a right turn, your vehicle must be:
options: a:As close to the right side of the road as practicable.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.,d:At the lane's centerline.
note: Position your vehicle far right in the lane when making a right turn; do not cut corners.

question: Does how fast you drive affect the distance your vehicle travels after you brake?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:
note: Faster speeds greatly increase stopping distances; higher speed means a longer distance to stop.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Controlled substances (illegal drugs or prescriptions),c:All of the above
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving and lead to DUII arrests.

question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:
options: a:Pay attention, obey signals, and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Assume no trains will come if no gates are down.,c:Drive around lowered gates if traffic is heavy.,d:Focus only on automobile traffic and ignore rail signals.
note: Obey all signals, look both ways, and never drive around lowered crossing gates when sharing roads with light rail.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A speed limit sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: The octagon shape is reserved for stop signs, signaling drivers must come to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop.,b:Keep driving in your lane at the same speed.,c:Slow down but remain in your lane.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping, taking care not to block intersections.

question: Is it safe to pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping?
options: a:False,b:True,c:
note: Never pull abruptly in front of a large vehicle that is slowing or stopping; the truck needs the space to brake safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?
options: a:Never; passing on the shoulder is prohibited.,b:When the shoulder is paved.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,d:When traffic is moving slowly.
note: Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and not permitted under any circumstances.

question: Can sudden wind gusts on highways create problems for all vehicles?
options: a:Can cause problems for all vehicles.,b:Only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:Only cause visibility problems.
note: Strong gusts of wind can affect vehicles of all sizes, sometimes reducing visibility and making vehicle control more difficult.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It causes concern about call cost.,b:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,c:It makes other drivers pay attention to you.
note: Cell phone use takes attention away from driving tasks—your hands, eyes, and mind are occupied, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you'll block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Never.,b:Only if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Only if you entered on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it before the light turns red; blocking intersections can lead to citations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to exceed the speed limit to complete a pass?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must not exceed the posted speed limit to finish a passing maneuver; always abide by speed limits when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway you should slow down:
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see a toll booth.
note: Join the exit lane in advance and reduce speed once you are in the exit lane, not on the mainline.

question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.,b:Use cruise control to keep steady speed.,c:Drive exactly as you would in normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, slow and make gradual changes; never use cruise control because you may lose control.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?
options: a:They can stay alert by opening a window or turning up the radio.,b:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they may appear to be drunk.,c:Drinking strong black coffee is enough to make them safe to drive.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving similarly to intoxication; temporary measures like fresh air or radio volume do not reliably restore alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:Drivers who do not stop.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle to arrive first proceeds first. If two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the right.

question: When another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction at night, what should your headlights be set to?
options: a:Low beam setting.,b:High beam setting.,c:Off; use parking lights only.,d:Alternate between high and low beams rapidly.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching another vehicle at night; switch to low beams to avoid blinding the other driver.

question: Which of the following should you NOT do when changing lanes?
options: a:Fail to check your side and rearview mirrors and blind spot.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:Check for drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors, signal your intention, and check blind spots; do not neglect these steps.

question: If you approach an intersection and the light turns yellow, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.
note: A solid yellow warns that the light will soon turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow the other vehicle?
options: a:At least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over.
note: On narrow roadways both drivers should allow sufficient space; you must allow at least half the main-traveled portion for oncoming traffic to pass safely.

question: If it begins to snow or sleet while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and allow extra following distance.,b:Approach other vehicles more quickly.,c:Ignore conditions and maintain usual distance.
note: Keep windows and mirrors clear and increase following distance; slippery roads require longer stopping distances.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, you should look:
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Directly at the headlights to signal them.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road and use peripheral vision to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.,b:When you are on a hill or curve.,c:When you are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
note: You may pass when the marking next to your lane is a broken line and it is safe to do so; never pass on hills, curves, or where a solid line is present.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: Be alert for children and pedestrians near school zones and crosswalks and be prepared to stop when necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do when a traffic control signal is not operating?
options: a:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop and come to a full stop.,b:If the intersection seems clear, proceed without stopping.,c:Speed through to clear the intersection quickly.
note: When signals are out, stop as you would at an all-way stop, then yield and proceed when it's safe.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, you should:
options: a:Gradually reduce speed, then steer gently back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Jerk the wheel to force back onto the road quickly.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.,d:Speed up to regain control.
note: Keep control by slowing down gradually off the pavement and then re-entering the roadway smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False,c:
note: It is always unlawful to exceed the posted speed limit, even while passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A solid red light with a left-turn sign.,d:A steady yellow light.
note: A steady green arrow gives protected turning movement; oncoming traffic must stop for turning vehicles.

question: To whom must you yield the right-of-way when a pedestrian is present?
options: a:Any pedestrian crossing any street.,b:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,c:Pedestrians only when the light is red.
note: Yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway at marked or unmarked crosswalks and exercise caution for anyone crossing any street.

question: Where are stop lines typically painted on the roadway?
options: a:Across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:Only in curves and on hills.,c:Next to churches and schools only.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks to indicate where vehicles must stop.

question: If you are in an intersection and hear an emergency vehicle using siren and lights, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,c:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop immediately.
note: If you are in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop to yield.

question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How can you reduce the risk of rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and let your vehicle slow before braking.,b:Always stop abruptly to signal following drivers.,c:Never check mirrors before stopping.
note: To help drivers behind you react, release the gas to slow, then apply steady pressure to the brakes so your brake lights warn following traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for a blind spot, then signal.,b:Only check your rearview mirror for traffic before moving.,c:Signal after you begin moving into the lane.,d:Assume no vehicles are in the other lane if mirrors look clear.
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder for vehicles in blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Turn on your flashers and continue at the same speed.,d:Drive to the nearest exit and stop there.
note: When emergency vehicles approach with sirens, move to the curb or edge of the roadway and stop until they pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic it is safest to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within posted limits.,b:Drive faster than the flow to get ahead.,c:Drive slower than everyone else to be safe.
note: Driving consistently with traffic flow and within limits reduces unexpected maneuvers and crash risk.

question: Before backing your vehicle, what steps should you take?
options: a:Walk completely around the vehicle and look front, sides, and rear before backing.,b:Depend only on your mirrors.,c:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.
note: Walk around to check for obstacles and then look front, sides, and over your shoulder while backing; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: Does safe passing depend on the cooperation of both drivers?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Passing safely requires cooperation: do not speed up when being passed and allow adequate room when reentering the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: After being stopped by police, a driver should immediately exit the vehicle and approach the officer's cruiser.
options: a:True,b:False
note: If stopped, remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the wheel unless the officer instructs you otherwise.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your vicinity, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel by pulling to the side when safe.,b:Speed up to avoid interaction.,c:Stop your vehicle immediately and block the lane.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, safely pull aside and clear a path so it can pass quickly and without obstruction.

question: When entering a roundabout you should slow and:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists, and to traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Yield only to vehicles in the roundabout.,c:Signal and enter without yielding to pedestrians.
note: Yield to pedestrians/bicyclists and give way to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing signals, you should:
options: a:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and ensure your vehicle can clear the tracks completely.,b:Cross immediately and quickly without looking.,c:Always stop before crossing regardless of conditions.
note: Check both directions and be sure there is room for your vehicle on the far side before crossing; never shift gears while on tracks.

question: Before making a turn you should:
options: a:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,b:Begin turning the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase speed to complete the turn faster.,d:Turn on hazard lights instead of signaling.
note: Signal about three to four seconds prior to turning so other drivers know your intentions.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet pavement, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on a wet surface; reduce speed to maintain tire traction and avoid hydroplaning.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than cars.,b:They rarely use headlights.,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.
note: Motorcycles are smaller, can be hidden in blind spots, and are harder to judge for speed and distance, so give them extra attention.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:A distracting activity that can reduce attention and control.,b:Beneficial for driver alertness.,c:Irrelevant to driving performance.,d:A required break activity on long trips.
note: Handling cigarettes or other items while driving takes attention and hands from the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Stop immediately even if in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal will change to red soon; stop if you can do so safely.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when it is safe to do so.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is never permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line between opposing lanes means drivers may pass if it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When may you cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway or street.,b:At any time to pass other vehicles.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: Solid yellow lines generally should not be crossed except to turn into driveways or side roads where permitted.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Because ramps and bridges are exposed to air on all sides, they can become icy before other roadway surfaces; use extra caution crossing them in freezing temperatures.

question: When driving at night, what is a recommended safety measure?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
note: Increase following distance at night to allow time to stop within the distance you can see; use high beams appropriately and avoid staring at oncoming lights.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles.,c:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles can block your view of the road ahead and prevent their drivers from seeing you; increasing your distance improves visibility and safety.

question: On possibly slippery roads you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.
note: Reduce speed and drive smoothly on slippery surfaces; do not use cruise control in these conditions.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash mean?
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol indicates the specified action is prohibited (e.g., no left turn).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your shoulder.,c:After about three seconds.
note: Wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and check blind spots before re-entering the lane.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn in front of the truck to beat it.,c:Try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb.
note: Do not try to squeeze between a large vehicle and the curb; wait until it finishes its turn to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Move into the lane belonging to oncoming traffic and pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Flash your lights to warn oncoming traffic.,c:Use the shoulder to pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane road often requires using the oncoming traffic lane; only pass when it is safe and legal.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:You cannot see as far as during daytime, making it hard to judge distance and speed.,b:There are more cars on the road at night.,c:The speed limit is always higher at night.,d:Headlights make it easier to judge speed.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles; you can see only as far as your headlights allow.

question: A green traffic arrow controlling a turn means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane may proceed only in the arrow's direction and has the right-of-way.,b:The arrow is equivalent to a circular green and you may go any direction.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light also appears.,d:The arrow applies only on one-way streets.
note: A green arrow permits movement in the direction shown and indicates that turning traffic has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop until a green light appears.,c:Continue at normal speed without change.
note: A flashing yellow means caution—slow down, watch for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed carefully.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on four-way flashers and continue slowly.,c:Turn on high beams and drive through.
note: If smoke obscures the road, slow, pull as far right off the roadway as you can, stop, and determine whether it's safe to continue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Continuously passing slower vehicles on a two-lane two-way road will:
options: a:Increase your risk of a collision.,b:Get you to your destination much more safely and quickly.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.,d:Always be legal if you signal.
note: Repeated passing on two-lane roads increases collision risk; avoid unnecessary passing.

question: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a multilane highway separated by a median, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.,b:Must stop until the school bus begins moving.,c:May continue driving because the median separates traffic.
note: When a divided highway has a median or physical barrier, traffic on the far side need not stop for a stopped school bus; otherwise all directions must stop.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift the vehicle into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,b:Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up.,c:Shift into park immediately.,d:Turn off your headlights and continue driving slowly.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, quickly shift into neutral, and brake steadily. Pull off the road when safe and then turn off the engine.

question: If you drink alcohol while taking medication, the result may be:
options: a:One negates the other.,b:The combination could multiply the impairing effects.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work better.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter drugs can intensify impairing effects and be dangerous.

question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead closely.,c:Pass other vehicles as soon as possible.
note: In work zones, increase your following distance and avoid tailgating to protect workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best mindset regarding right-of-way rules?
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,b:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume most drivers obey the rules so you can proceed quickly.
note: Never assume others will yield; be ready to give up your legal right-of-way if doing so prevents a crash.

question: What important action should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Speed up to complete the turn quickly.,c:Always move into the left lane before turning.,d:Close your windows.
note: Before turning, look to the rear and both sides to ensure it's safe, and adjust speed to complete the turn safely.

question: How should small children ride in a vehicle to be safe?
options: a:Be secured in an appropriate child safety seat.,b:Be safely held by a strong adult.,c:Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
note: Children who are too small for adult seat belts must use child restraint systems appropriate for their size and age; holding a child is not safe.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights until you are 10 feet behind.,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.,d:Alternate between high and low beams.
note: Use low beams when following closely behind another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol’s effects from your body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, showers, or exercise do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: Before you enter an intersection, in what sequence should you look?
options: a:Left, then right, then left again.,b:Only to the left.,c:Only to the right.,d:Down at your speedometer then forward.
note: Look left, right, then left again before entering an intersection to detect nearby hazards and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
