options: a:They are removed if you have one outside mirror on each side.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:They can be checked only with rearview mirrors.
note: Mirrors don't eliminate blind spots; large trucks have especially large no-zones that other drivers should avoid.

question: When are roads most likely to be very slippery after rain begins?
options: a:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:After it has been raining steadily for several hours.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Road surfaces can become especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rainfall as oils on the pavement rise to the surface.

question: Which of the following helps you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance to allow more reaction time.,b:Ignore headlights and keep using high beams.,c:Drive only with parking lights on.,d:Depend on interior lights to see controls.
note: At night, reduce speed, increase following distance, and ensure headlights are working properly to improve safety.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene at all costs.,c:Leave the injured where they are and drive to get help.
note: Do not move injured persons unnecessarily; movement can worsen injuries. Keep them warm, render first aid if trained, and wait for medical personnel.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Straight ahead.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: If oncoming headlights blind you, look to the right side of the roadway ahead to reduce glare while staying aware of the lane limits.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription is safe to use while driving.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; it is unlawful to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid red light.
note: A red flashing traffic light means stop, just like a stop sign. Proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Always keep your eyes focused only straight ahead.,c:Turn off the radio and avoid scanning mirrors.
note: Use continuous observation—front, sides, and rear—so you can anticipate hazards and adjust speed or position as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of lights on a vertical traffic signal?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On vertical traffic signals red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, you should:
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.,b:Keep instrument panel lights very bright so others see you.,c:Use high beams to better see the road ahead.
note: Reduce speed at night so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Do not return to the driving lane until you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check for traffic when entering a freeway?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder in the direction of the merge.,b:Only use your rearview mirror.,c:Use your rearview and side mirrors without turning your head.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use mirrors and a quick shoulder check to detect vehicles in your blind spot and choose a safe gap.

question: In fog, you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers primarily.
note: Low beams improve visibility in fog; high beams reflect and worsen visibility.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what should you do before you leave?
options: a:Plan your route in advance.,b:Depend only on road signs to find your way.,c:Start with a general idea and figure it out while driving.
note: Plan your trip ahead of time and check maps or directions so you do not rely solely on unfamiliar road signs while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Drivers may pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
options: a:True,b:False
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited. Passing is allowed only when the broken line is on your side.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes, the safest method is to:
options: a:Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Pass quickly and close to the cyclist to minimize lane time.,c:Never pass until a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Give cyclists at least 3 feet (more at higher speeds) and only pass when it's safe with no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you're on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Keep driving until you reach the next block.,c:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep moving.
note: On a one-way street, pull to the nearest edge of the roadway and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are on a one-way street; you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on that street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on that street moves to the left.
note: You may turn left from one one-way street to another one-way street if traffic on the destination street flows leftward and no sign prohibits the turn.

question: As blood alcohol increases, it generally:
options: a:Slows your reactions and increases errors.,b:Makes you feel less confident but speeds reactions.,c:Causes the body to metabolize alcohol faster.
note: Higher blood alcohol concentration slows reactions, impairs judgment, and increases risky behavior.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the wheels sharply to get back on immediately.,c:Accelerate and then swerve back onto the pavement.
note: Slow down gradually while holding the wheel steady, check traffic, then re-enter the roadway when safe.

question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Drink coffee and continue.,c:Open a window and drive on.,d:Turn on bright lights to stay awake.
note: Resting or switching drivers is the best way to address driving fatigue.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by easing off the gas pedal.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and do not brake until under control; then brake gently and pull off the road.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your lights to signal them to hurry.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Slow and prepare to stop; always yield to pedestrians and be especially cautious near children.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance when visibility or stopping time is reduced: behind large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when tailgated.

question: To prevent "expressway hypnosis" on long trips you should:
options: a:Keep your eyes moving and vary speed occasionally.,b:Keep the interior very warm.,c:Stare straight ahead to maintain focus.
note: Avoid staring at one spot; vary speed slightly, scan the roadway, and take regular breaks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must pull over and stop:
options: a:Regardless of its direction of approach.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop for emergency vehicles with lights or sirens, no matter which direction they come from.

question: At a railroad crossing where you see no train, you must stop under which condition?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:Only if crossing lights are flashing.,c:If a flagger is signaling you to stop.
note: You must stop for railroad crossings if a stop sign is posted, lights are flashing, gates lowered, a flagger directs you, or a train is obviously near.

question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph may take up to how many feet to stop?
options: a:Approximately 125 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:Nearly 400 feet.
note: Large trucks require much longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles; a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph can take almost 400 feet to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver who signals first.
note: At an open intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic, what is the likely result?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic and could receive a ticket.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly slower than the normal flow can block traffic and may lead to a citation; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to:
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A slow sign.,d:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to other traffic, like a stop sign.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane to move into, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Brake hard to warn the tailgater.,c:Ignore the tailgater and maintain speed at all costs.
note: If no right lane exists, slow gradually when safe to allow the tailgater to pass; never brake abruptly.

question: Diamond-shaped traffic signs are used to:
options: a:Warn of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Indicate public recreation areas.,c:Alert drivers to school zones specifically.
note: Diamond-shaped signs typically warn of road hazards or changing road conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Both may proceed together without yielding.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A dashed yellow line indicates two-way traffic and that passing is allowed for the side with the dashed line when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how much space should you leave between your vehicle and the cars in front and behind?
options: a:Two feet,b:Six inches,c:One foot
note: When parallel parking you should leave at least two feet between your vehicle and the cars parked in front and behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you come to an intersection that is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass completely through.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking the intersection is illegal and dangerous.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:High beam headlights regardless of other traffic.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as daylight fades; use high beams only where no other vehicles are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the first available lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel into the first available legal lane on the one-way street.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, it indicates:
options: a:The road is narrowing ahead.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left ahead.
note: An edge line angling inward shows the road will become narrower ahead; reduce speed and take care.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side of the road.,d:The left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping your lane position.

question: You should use your horn to warn others when:
options: a:Passing a bicyclist.,b:Traveling through an intersection.,c:You see a child who might run into the street.
note: Use the horn as a warning if a child or other road user is about to enter danger and may not see you.

question: Never use high beam headlights in fog because:
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Approaching vehicles won't see you.,c:Vehicles behind will follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce your visibility; use low beams instead.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull off at the first safe location and take a break.,b:Try to fight the drowsiness and continue driving.,c:Take caffeine pills and keep driving.,d:Open the windows and turn up the radio to stay awake.
note: When tired, stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers; caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

question: What minimum following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle in normal conditions?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three to four seconds.
note: Allow at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle to give extra stopping distance and reaction time if the rider falls or swerves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to create space in front so the other driver can complete the pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Maintain speed and ignore their attempt.
note: When another driver signals to pass, slow slightly to increase the gap ahead and help them re-enter safely.

question: What does 'distracted driving' mean?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: Distracted driving includes anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving and increases crash risk.

question: When a pedestrian uses a guide dog or white cane and is crossing, you must:
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way.,b:Tell them where to cross.,c:Only yield if at a corner.
note: Always yield to pedestrians who are blind or using guide dogs or white canes; they must be given the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it true you do not have to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing if it is on a private road?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm even on private roads.

question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as which traffic control?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign always.,c:No control; you may proceed without slowing.
note: A crossbuck indicates a railroad crossing and should be treated like a yield sign: slow, look, and yield to any approaching trains.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Always change lanes gradually and only when necessary, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross double solid yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:Only to turn into a driveway or private entrance
note: You may not cross double solid yellow lines to pass. Crossing is allowed only when turning into or out of a driveway or private entrance, not for passing.

question: Blue traffic signs give information about what?
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas, hospitals, and food.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information like distances to locations.
note: Blue highway signs are service signs that indicate motorist facilities and services.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross the centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.,b:If the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,c:If the yellow line next to your side is broken.
note: You may pass only when the broken yellow line is on your side of the centerline and it is safe to do so; a broken line next to your lane indicates passing is allowed.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Following other vehicles too closely,c:Excessive speed under conditions
note: Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and tailgating are all common causes of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit outside a business or residential area is:
options: a:45 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: On state roads outside business or residential areas, the typical default speed is 45 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers who are turning left must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Oncoming cars traveling straight ahead.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:No one.
note: A vehicle turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight; only turn when the maneuver can be made safely without affecting oncoming vehicles.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One drink.,b:Two drinks.,c:Three drinks.
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair driving; even a single drink can reduce your ability to drive safely.

question: If the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk — there may be pedestrians you cannot see; wait until all pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

question: Which of these may cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Talking or texting on a cell phone.,c:Changing a radio station or CD.,d:All of the above.
note: Many everyday tasks can distract drivers from the road; distractions increase crash risk and should be avoided.

question: When should drivers use their turn signals?
options: a:When changing lanes, entering/exiting the freeway, or turning at intersections.,b:Only when turning at an intersection.,c:Only when changing lanes.
note: Always signal before lane changes, freeway entry/exit, and turns so other road users can respond.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you begin to pass another vehicle if you do not have space to return to your lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Do not start to pass unless you know you have enough space to return to your lane safely; do not rely on other drivers to make room.

question: If a road is slippery, your following distance should be:
options: a:Greater than normal.,b:The same as usual.,c:Closer than normal.
note: Slippery conditions require increased following distance to allow more stopping time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an unmarked stop sign (no crosswalk), where should you stop?
options: a:True,b:False
note: At a stop sign you must stop at the stop line, if present; if not, stop before entering the crosswalk or, if none, before entering the intersection.

question: If a pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your signal turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
note: At a green light you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk; wait for them to clear the roadway before proceeding.

question: You hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see where the vehicle is.,b:Slow down and continue driving until you locate it.,c:Pull safely to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.
note: If you hear a siren or air horn and don't know the location of the emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right and stop until you are certain it is not headed toward you.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot refers to an area:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head.,b:You see in your rearview mirror.,c:Directly behind your vehicle only.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle you cannot see using mirrors alone; check by turning your head.

question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Slow down and pass while watching for children.,d:Proceed if you think children are not present.
note: Stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate:
options: a:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:Passing is permitted if safe.,c:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean drivers in either direction may not cross the centerline to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start the turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane if it looks clear.,c:The center lane only.
note: Begin left turns from the far left lane when turning from one one-way street onto another one-way street.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate them.,b:Flash your headlights to make them aware of you.,c:Always pass on the right side quickly.
note: Large vehicles have big blind spots to their sides and rear; avoid lingering beside them and give extra space when passing.

question: While backing up, what is the recommended way to see behind your vehicle?
options: a:Look over your shoulder and out the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors.,b:Rely exclusively on your mirrors.,c:Open your door to check behind you.,d:Back up while looking forward.
note: Turn your head and look through the rear window when backing; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: Parking in an access aisle next to a handicap spot is allowed when:
options: a:Never.,b:When you have a disability placard.,c:When other spaces are full.
note: Access aisles are for wheelchair access and must remain clear; parking there is prohibited and fined.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal means:
options: a:A steady red light will soon appear.,b:A flashing yellow will appear next.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will change to red soon; slow and prepare to stop if safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When your lane is next to a broken yellow line and it is safe to pass.,b:In a curve or on a hill.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass only where permitted (e.g., a broken yellow line adjacent to your lane) and only when it is safe; never pass on hills, curves, or on the shoulder.

question: If the rear of your vehicle starts skidding to the left, what action should you take?
options: a:Steer to the left.,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,c:Steer to the right.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, remove your foot from the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go — for a rear skid to the left, steer left to regain control.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night, reducing reaction time and visibility.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night regardless of visibility.,d:Headlights eliminate all visibility issues.
note: Reduced visibility and headlight glare limit how far ahead you can see at night, increasing hazard risk.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) signs indicate?
options: a:School zones and school crossings.,b:Speed limits.,c:No passing zones.
note: A pentagonal sign indicates you are in a school zone or near a school crossing; be especially alert for children and pedestrians.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make constant visual checks and be alert.,c:Always slow down to a stop near them.
note: Motorcycles are easily hidden in blind spots; regularly scan and check mirrors and blind spots to ensure you see them.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,c:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
note: Coffee may make you feel more alert but it does not affect the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream or make you sober.

question: At a steady yellow traffic light, if you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop before the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal will change to red; stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Signal early enough so others know your intent.,b:Only signal just before changing lanes.,c:Signal after you have completed the pass.,d:Not signal at all if traffic is light.
note: Signal in plenty of time before passing so other road users are aware of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.
note: A traffic officer's directions override traffic signals, signs, and markings and must be followed.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Stand in traffic lanes to direct cars.,c:Leave immediately if the other vehicle is blocking your path.
note: Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, do not stand in lanes of traffic, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk before changing lanes instead of checking.,d:Change lanes without signaling.
note: Turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction of your move to make sure the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: A curb painted red means:
options: a:No parking, standing, or stopping.,b:Loading zone only.,c:Reserved for passenger drop-off.
note: Red curbs indicate areas where stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited.

question: Do solid or dashed white pavement markings indicate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:False,b:True
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased.,b:No interaction will occur.,c:Both effects will be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and cause unpredictable effects; even small amounts can become dangerous.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn off the ignition (carefully), apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe area.,b:Blow your horn repeatedly to warn other drivers.,c:Slam on the brakes hard to stop immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, brake as needed, turn off the ignition (without locking the steering), and steer to a safe area; then stop and address the issue.

question: If you are parallel parked facing downhill, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the side of the road or curb.,b:Turn them away from the curb.,c:Leave them straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or road edge so the car will roll into it if it moves.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid red arrow means vehicles in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in that direction until the signal changes.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it and then stop to the right.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks you should:
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,b:Cross as soon as one train passes.,c:Stop on the first track and then move forward, watching for other trains.,d:Assume only one train will come through.
note: At multiple-track crossings, do not proceed until you can see down all tracks and confirm no other trains are approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning onto a street that has multiple lanes traveling in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Into the lane marked with an arrow.,c:Into the middle lane.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, complete the turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Road or weather conditions make normal speeds unsafe.,b:You see a police car, even if conditions are fine.,c:Entering a highway with other cars.
note: Reduce speed when conditions are less than ideal, even if the posted limit is higher.

question: Each time you pass another vehicle, what happens to your risk of collision?
options: a:There is no change in collision risk.,b:There is an increased chance of collision.,c:The chance of collision decreases.
note: Passing always increases the chance of collision; only pass when you are certain it is safe and you have enough room.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed and prepare to yield.,b:Maintain your current speed.,c:Increase your speed to merge quickly.
note: Slow down when approaching a roundabout; travel at low speeds and yield to circulating traffic.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: Avoid deep puddles when possible; driving through them can cause loss of control or vehicle damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does the absence of a sign or pavement marking forbidding passing mean it is safe to pass?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Lack of markings does not guarantee a safe passing opportunity; you must judge visibility, oncoming traffic, and road conditions before passing.

question: Is it legal to park in the handicap parking access aisle next to a marked stall?
options: a:False,b:True,c:
note: Parking in the access aisle is prohibited; these spaces are reserved for wheelchair access and lifts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe to pass other vehicles?
options: a:At intersections.,b:On straight rural roads.,c:In open countryside.
note: Passing is dangerous at intersections, railroad crossings, and entrances where other vehicles or pedestrians might enter the roadway; avoid passing there.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take the time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,b:Drive faster because you are more alert.,c:Drive no differently than usual.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair driving; pause and regain composure before driving.

question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should:
options: a:Drive more slowly and turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your parking lights only.,c:Use only emergency flashers and keep speed constant.
note: When visibility is reduced by dust or smoke, slow down and turn on headlights so others can see you.

question: A broken (dashed) yellow line between two lanes indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted when safe.,b:Traffic lanes go the same direction only.,c:Passing is prohibited.
note: Dashed yellow centerlines mean passing is allowed if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

question: In heavy fog you should:
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,c:Turn lights on and off to warn others.
note: Use low beams in fog; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: When you need to change lanes, what important steps should you take?
options: a:Signal ahead of the lane change, check your blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear.,b:Honk before changing lanes only.,c:Speed up and merge quickly.,d:Flash headlights and change lanes without signaling.
note: Always signal in advance, check blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:A slow-moving vehicle (traveling 25 mph or less).,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:There is shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange-red reflective triangle marks a slow-moving vehicle such as a tractor or certain maintenance equipment; use caution.

question: After a stressful incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before beginning to drive.,b:Play loud music to distract yourself.,c:Drive fast on a highway to release stress.,d:Immediately start driving to get home quicker.
note: If upset or distracted, give yourself time to cool off; emotional distraction impairs driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: During school hours, what is the speed limit in a school zone?
options: a:25 mph,b:10 mph,c:15 mph
note: A five-sided sign marks a school zone. During specified hours and when children are present, the speed limit is 15 mph; drive carefully when children are nearby.

question: When involved in a collision, what should you do regarding the injured?
options: a:Do not move seriously injured persons unless there's immediate danger.,b:Move injured people as far from the road as possible regardless of injuries.,c:Assume injured people are fine and don't call for help.
note: Avoid moving seriously injured persons unless necessary to prevent further immediate danger; call for medical help and render aid if trained.

question: You drive defensively when you:
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
note: Defensive driving means scanning the road and surroundings continuously to anticipate hazards rather than staring only at the vehicle directly ahead.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Remain inside your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Leave the vehicle and walk for assistance.,c:Lie down inside the car and sleep.,d:Walk into the road to attract attention.
note: Stay in your vehicle, keep warm, and wait for rescue; leaving the car in a storm is hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must obey directions given by which of the following people?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: You must follow instructions from authorized traffic-control persons such as flaggers, police, and other designated traffic directors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing directions, you may:
options: a:Cross the lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross the lines to pass slower traffic if no oncoming cars are visible.,c:Never cross under any circumstance including left turns.,d:Use the left lane for passing anytime traffic allows.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; cross only to make permitted left turns into private roads or driveways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a roundabout or traffic circle you should generally be in:
options: a:The right lane unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.,b:The left lane at all times.,c:The center lane and signal early.
note: Use the right lane to exit a roundabout unless pavement markings or signs require otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the light is green but traffic ahead is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and follow the vehicles ahead.,b:Remain out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: Even with a green signal, do not enter an intersection if you cannot completely clear it. Blocking the intersection can impede cross traffic and may result in a citation.

question: What does a red right-turn arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may not turn in that direction until the signal turns green.,b:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:You may turn in that direction only after coming to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means ''stop.'' You must remain stopped and may not turn in that direction until a green light or green arrow appears.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly while slowing.,b:Apply the brake and hold it hard.,c:Immediately pull over at high speed.
note: Keep control, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently to slow before pulling off the road.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions or exceeding the posted limit.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Constantly scanning and staying focused.,d:Maintaining the speed of surrounding traffic within the limit.
note: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions are frequent contributors to crashes.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose surfaces and whenever traction or visibility is reduced.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:The driver and all passengers in the vehicle.,b:Only the front-seat passengers.,c:Only passengers on long trips.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts; unbelted passengers become projectiles in a crash.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:Your high-beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low-beam headlights (and fog lights if available).
note: Use low-beam headlights and fog lights if equipped. High beams can reflect off fog and reduce visibility further.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles can stop much more quickly than standard vehicles, so following too closely increases crash risk.,b:Motorcycles do not follow the same traffic laws as other vehicles.,c:Motorcycles always brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop rapidly; following too closely reduces your time to react if the motorcyclist brakes or swerves, increasing the risk of collision.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Having one outside mirror eliminates blind spots.,b:Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, blind spots remain. Large trucks have particularly large blind zones that drivers should avoid.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:More dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare, and a higher likelihood of impaired or tired drivers.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate compared with a circular yellow light?
options: a:It has the same meaning; you must reduce speed and prepare for red.,b:It means you may turn freely without yielding.,c:It indicates lane closure ahead.,d:It signals a pedestrian crossing only.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending; treat it like a circular yellow and prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle whose driver honks first.,d:The vehicle that arrives second.
note: At intersections of similar roads with no controls, you must yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, you must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:No one, you have the right-of-way.,c:Only vehicles turning right.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists in the intersection.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Eating fatty foods.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing else speeds up sobering.

question: An advisory or speed restriction sign attached to a curve usually:
options: a:Shows a recommended speed and should not be ignored in wet, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:Is triangular in shape.,c:Is blue with black lettering.,d:May be disregarded in poor weather if you feel comfortable.
note: Advisory speed signs indicate suggested safe speeds for curves; reduce speed further in adverse weather.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to watch the road.,b:Look directly at the headlights to signal them.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: Avoid staring at oncoming high beams; glance to the right edge of the road and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Both watch for a second train and wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.,b:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing only.,c:Look for a second train only.
note: Even after one train passes, check for additional trains and do not proceed until gates are raised and all warning signals have ceased.

question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or without warning.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Avoid sudden lane changes; always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before moving.

question: True or false: Pedestrians in crosswalks and intersections always have the right-of-way.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks at intersections, but 'always' can be misleading in some controlled situations; yield when pedestrians are crossing.

question: Are you required to obey directions given by a school crossing guard?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Always obey crossing guards and posted signs in school zones. Slow down and stop when directed for children’s safety.

question: Which medications might negatively affect driving?
options: a:Any medication that can cause drowsiness or impair cognition.,b:Only headache medicines.,c:Only diet pills.
note: Any medication—prescription or over-the-counter—can impair driving. Check labels and consult a pharmacist or doctor about side effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous on some roads.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:Vehicle speed does not affect safety.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can create hazards as other drivers may attempt unsafe passes; travel with the flow within legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you must:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn regardless of conditions.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and any pedestrians before making a left turn.

question: What do regulatory signs tell drivers?
options: a:What drivers must or must not do in a specific area.,b:About nearby scenic or recreational sites.,c:Warn of conditions ahead.,d:Only indicate speed limits but nothing else.
note: Regulatory signs, usually rectangular and white, indicate laws and regulations such as speed limits, turn prohibitions, and parking rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but lacks a stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it's safe.,b:After slowing to check for cross traffic without stopping.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection every time.,d:Without stopping if no cross traffic is visible.
note: Stop before entering the intersection when a stop sign is present, even if no stop line or crosswalk exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:From the left lane.,b:From the middle of the intersection.,c:From the right lane.
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, begin the turn from the leftmost lane.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Use your four-way flashers and move off the road to a safe place.,b:Sit in your car and wait without signaling.,c:Sound your horn at passing drivers for help.
note: Turn on hazard flashers, get the vehicle as far off the road as possible, and signal for assistance safely.

question: Slowing down to look at a crash or other unusual event typically:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion and can increase crash risk.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow.,d:Is recommended to get a better view.
note: 'Rubbernecking' slows traffic and contributes to congestion and secondary collisions; avoid it.

question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Shift to a low gear before descending steep hills and allow extra following distance.,b:Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.,c:Brake abruptly to avoid sliding.,d:Use cruise control to maintain speed.
note: Use low gear on steep descents, increase following distance, and pump brakes unless ABS is present.

question: What is the primary purpose of barriers, drums, cones, and signs in work zones?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: Work zone traffic control devices are used to protect workers and to channel traffic safely around hazards and work areas.

question: Why can driving at night be more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:It is more likely to be raining at night.
note: Darkness reduces your field of vision and ability to judge distance and speed; use proper headlights and reduce speed to compensate.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: Steer toward the direction you want the vehicle to go, and once it begins to straighten, correct the steering back.

question: Which of the following should you do when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: At night, increase following distance and use headlights appropriately; do not stare at oncoming high beams to avoid being blinded by glare.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance.,b:Drive more slowly than usual.,c:Be ready to use your horn.
note: Maintain at least a three- to four-second following distance behind a motorcyclist to allow time to react if the rider must stop or falls.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you begin reducing your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,d:Only after exiting the ramp.
note: Maintain freeway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then begin slowing to the posted advisory speed for the exit ramp.

question: While driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.,c:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be ready to stop in work zones; hazards and workers may be present.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians have the right-of-way and vehicles must yield.,b:Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.,d:Pedestrians must always wait for vehicles to pass.
note: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way; vehicles must stop when required.

question: Should you use high-beam headlights in fog, heavy rain, or snow?
options: a:No — use low beams in fog, snow, and heavy rain.,b:Yes — high beams improve visibility in precipitation.
note: High beams reflect off precipitation and worsen glare; use low beams in fog, heavy rain, or snow.

question: What is the legal blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for a person age 21 or older?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers age 21 and older, operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal and dangerous.

question: A 'Merging lanes' sign is intended to tell drivers to:
options: a:Be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge.,b:Come to a complete stop before merging.,c:Speed up to prevent merging traffic from entering.,d:Ignore other vehicles when merging.
note: Merging lanes signs indicate that two lanes will soon merge into one and drivers should be ready to change lanes or allow others to merge.

question: Always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley.,b:Only when turning at an intersection.,c:Only when other vehicles are nearby.
note: Use turn signals to communicate intentions before lane changes, parking maneuvers, and entering traffic from alleys or driveways.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your right foot for both acceleration and braking.,b:Use your left foot for braking.,c:Always use both feet simultaneously.,d:Alternate feet depending on speed.
note: Use the right foot for both to avoid accidentally pressing both pedals simultaneously; brake smoothly.

question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:Excessive oil use.,c:Only increased vehicle noise.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment, posing a deadly risk; repair immediately.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Only lock the doors.,c:Leave the engine running if warm.,d:Just set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock it, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: If the rear of your vehicle starts to skid left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, and steer into the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: You should yield to a pedestrian:
options: a:At all times if needed to avoid striking them.,b:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when pedestrian signals favor them.
note: Always do what you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, yielding even if they are not obeying traffic laws when necessary to prevent a collision.

question: What does a flashing yellow X lane-use signal mean?
options: a:You may use the indicated lane only to complete a left turn.,b:The lane is closed to all traffic.,c:The signal is about to change to a red X.,d:You must speed up to clear the lane.
note: A flashing yellow X indicates that the lane is for left turns only; it warns that the lane is not for through travel.

question: When is walking or standing on the traveled portion of an expressway permitted?
options: a:When your car has stalled.,b:When you are trying to wave down another car.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Do not stop or walk on the traveled lanes of an expressway except for emergencies; if your vehicle stalls, remain off the roadway and call for help.

question: When roads are slippery, what adjustment should you make to your following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery surfaces you need more time and distance to stop, so increase the gap between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or the vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination, reducing a driver’s ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing an unprotected railroad track, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have enough space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,b:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,c:You have the right-of-way and do not need to look for trains.
note: Do not enter railroad tracks unless there is room for your vehicle to fully clear them on the far side; never pass another vehicle on the tracks.

question: At night it is hardest to see:
options: a:Pedestrians,b:Road signs,c:Other motorists
note: Pedestrians are the most difficult to see at night compared with signs or other vehicles.

question: Consistently looking far down the highway while driving helps you do what?
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Helps you keep up with traffic.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Scanning far ahead lets you anticipate hazards and make smoother, safer driving decisions with less sudden braking or steering.

question: What is the safest approach to crossing a railroad track?
options: a:Listen, look both directions, and proceed only if it is safe.,b:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey crossing signals; never assume the tracks are clear until you are sure it is safe.

question: True or false: The faster your vehicle is moving, the longer it takes to stop after reacting to unexpected movements by other drivers.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Higher speeds increase reaction and stopping distances, so traveling faster gives you less time to respond to hazards.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error,b:New drivers,c:Bad weather
note: Most collisions occur because of mistakes or poor decisions by drivers, such as failing to see other road users or reacting improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and drive through cautiously without stopping.,c:Wait for a flashing green light before proceeding.,d:Turn right only.
note: A flashing red light is like a stop sign: stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when safe.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in precipitation you can help others see you by turning on:
options: a:Your headlights,b:Your parking lights only,c:The instrument panel lights
note: Use headlights when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: To increase visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog to improve both your visibility and others' ability to see you.

question: A double solid yellow line down the center of the road means passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed in one direction only.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate two-way traffic and that passing is prohibited for vehicles in either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it safer to cross as few lanes as possible when making a turn?
options: a:True,b:False
note: The safest turning technique is to cross the minimum number of lanes necessary: start in the lane closest to your destination and turn into the first legal lane.

question: To avoid last-minute braking and turning, you should look how far ahead of your vehicle?
options: a:10 to 15 seconds,b:One to three seconds,c:Five to seven seconds
note: Scan the road 10 to 15 seconds ahead to anticipate hazards and avoid sudden maneuvers.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time and increases the risk of rear-end collisions if traffic stops suddenly.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what actions should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer to the right, and brake firmly.,b:Steer left and accelerate to avoid contact.,c:Turn off your lights and flash them rapidly.,d:Speed up and swerve into oncoming traffic.
note: Honk to draw attention, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly and steadily if a collision seems unavoidable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, how should you control your speed?
options: a:Drive much more slowly than usual.,b:Drive faster than usual.
note: Backing is harder to control and stop; back no faster than a slow walking speed and look carefully in all directions.

question: Which technique is most important to avoid crashes when roads are icy or snowy?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: Reducing speed and increasing following distance are the most effective ways to avoid crashes on snow- or ice-covered roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule for passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
note: Passing increases crash risk; stay with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and only pass when necessary and safe.

question: You should avoid driving beside large vehicles for extended periods because:
options: a:They have large blind spots on both sides.,b:They drive much slower than cars.,c:They always signal early when changing lanes.
note: Large vehicles have extensive blind spots; it's safer to drop back or move ahead rather than stay alongside.

question: Construction zone signs are typically what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black lettering.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of road work.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:One standard alcoholic drink per hour.,b:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
note: On average the body metabolizes about one standard drink per hour, though many factors (weight, food, health) affect this rate.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates:
options: a:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,b:Yield and be prepared to stop if necessary.,c:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign—slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'No stopping' sign means you may stop only for which reason?
options: a:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,b:To unload packages.,c:To discharge passengers.
note: A No Stopping sign allows stopping only to obey a traffic control device, follow an officer's directions, or to prevent a conflict with other traffic.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor safety issue.,c:Safe if you've had only a couple of drinks.,d:Acceptable if you drive slowly.
note: Driving under the influence endangers everyone and is a major safety issue.

question: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; two solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow with black markings.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are yellow (often diamond-shaped) with black symbols or lettering; they warn of potential hazards or changes in road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed typically:
options: a:Increases the likelihood of serious injury or death.,b:Saves significant travel time.,c:Helps maneuver around obstacles safely.
note: Excessive speed contributes heavily to crash severity and fatalities; it rarely saves meaningful time and increases risk.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:Only when driving on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing.,b:When the bus is parked on the shoulder with no one aboard.,c:Whenever the bus approaches even if its lights are not flashing.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic from both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and is loading or unloading children.

question: When parked uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs—including sedatives, some cough medicines, and marijuana—can impair driving ability.

question: You are about to turn right and a person with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. You should:
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before turning.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until they cross.,d:Edge around them slowly while they cross.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait for them to cross.

question: Which factor significantly affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel, etc.).,b:Signal lights ahead.,c:The time of day.
note: Road surface and conditions greatly affect braking performance; reduce speed when roads are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you may:
options: a:Cross the centerline to change lanes when safe.,b:Only drive within your lane at all times.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: What should you keep in mind when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.,b:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Tires have reduced traction on loose gravel and dirt; slow down, allow more distance to stop, and take turns more gently to avoid skids.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:Depressant.,b:Stimulant.,c:Antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment and slows reaction times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you should:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars.,c:Pull out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.
note: Yield to all pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway before entering from a private road or driveway.

question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your lane only when:
options: a:The entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.,b:You can no longer see the vehicle in your side mirror.,c:Two seconds have passed since beginning the pass.,d:You cross directly in front of the passed vehicle's hood.
note: Do not move back until the entire vehicle passed is visible in your rearview mirror.

question: When passing a large truck, what should a driver of a smaller vehicle be ready for?
options: a:Gusts of wind that can affect your steering.,b:Loud noises only.,c:Extra exhaust pollution.
note: Large vehicles can create strong wind gusts that may move smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering.

question: Which of the following can be a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, erratic speed, abrupt lane changes, and sudden stops—any of which could indicate a drunk driver.

question: Why should you look farther ahead when driving on a freeway compared with a city street?
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:To spot potential hazards early.
note: Highway traffic moves faster and changes quickly; looking further ahead lets you detect hazards, merging vehicles, and traffic flow changes sooner.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in traffic on a highway, what should you do?
options: a:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,b:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,c:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.
note: Always check behind and to the sides, then observe the traffic ahead to select a safe gap before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best practice when merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge smoothly.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Turn on hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.,d:Stop at the end of the on-ramp and wait for an opening.
note: Entering traffic must yield, so use the on-ramp to reach freeway speed and blend in smoothly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another car, you have enough space to return to your lane when:
options: a:You can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals you to return.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, showing a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: Do not make sudden lane changes or illegal turns to get back to an exit. Proceed to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum (or minimum) speed under ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions require it.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Nighttime reduces visibility making cyclists harder to see; both motorists and bicyclists should be especially cautious after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must:
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,b:Slow and proceed with caution if you think you can beat it.,c:Cross at your own risk if no lights are flashing.
note: Never attempt to cross if a train is near; wait until it has completely passed and the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the legal right-of-way at an intersection, what is the safest action?
options: a:Proceed immediately because you have the right-of-way.,b:Check for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before moving.,c:Assume others will yield to you.
note: Even with the right-of-way, always scan for pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles; yield if necessary to avoid collisions.

question: You discover a defect that could affect safe operation of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive more slowly until you can afford to fix it.,c:Delay repairs until it becomes severe.
note: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be repaired before driving the vehicle. Fix it as soon as possible.

question: Guide (destination) signs are typically what color?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide signs have a green background and provide directional and mileage information to specific destinations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:When you cannot see any vehicle directly to your right.
note: You may safely return to your original lane after passing when you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating adequate space.

question: After a minor collision with no injuries and little damage at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Leave your vehicle where it stopped until police arrive.,c:Not move your vehicle at any cost.
note: If safe and feasible, move vehicles out of traffic to avoid causing additional hazards or congestion.

question: Which of the following is illegal for a passenger in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Use a cell phone.,b:Sleep.,c:Have an opened alcohol container.
note: Possessing or consuming an open alcoholic beverage in a motor vehicle on a public road is unlawful and can result in penalties for driver and passengers.

question: True or False: A motorist making a left turn must yield to oncoming bicyclists.
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles in the same way you would yield to oncoming vehicles.

question: Are most work zone signs orange in color?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Work zone signs are generally orange (often diamond-shaped) and reflective to alert drivers to construction and maintenance activities.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Drivers may change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions.,d:You must stop before crossing it.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a painted stop line at an intersection, you should stop:
options: a:Before the stop line.,b:On top of the stop line.,c:Past the stop line into the intersection.
note: Stop before the painted stop line to allow pedestrians a clear walkway and to obey traffic control markings.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to finish sooner.,c:Turn up the radio and drive on.,d:Open all windows and drive faster.
note: When drowsy, stop in a safe area and rest; driving tired is dangerous.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the wheel.
note: Position your hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain control and perform safe turns.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving.,b:Work zones are marked with black and white signs.,c:You do not need to slow down when approaching a work zone.
note: Work zones can be stationary or involve moving operations (like line striping or mowing). They are typically marked with orange signs and you must slow down and pay close attention.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing and there is no traffic light?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.,d:The faster party must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing intersections without traffic lights; the driver must yield even when turning.

question: What message is displayed on a red octagonal sign?
